intramuscular
/ˌɪntrəˈmʌskjʊlə(r)/
核心：（医学）肌肉内的、肌注的 —— 说注射。
① The vaccine is given as an intramuscular injection in the upper arm.
= 那种疫苗是在上臂作肌肉注射。
an intramuscular injection = 肌肉注射
说注射的部位：打进肌肉里，而不是皮下或血管里。
② Some painkillers work faster when they are given by intramuscular injection rather than as tablets.
= 有些止痛药用肌肉注射比吃药片起效快。
by intramuscular injection = 通过肌肉注射

intranet
/ˈɪntrənet/
核心：（公司内部的）内联网 —— 只供一个组织内部使用的网络。
① All the forms you need can be found on the company intranet.
= 你需要的所有表格都能在公司内联网上找到。
the company intranet = 公司内联网
② The school uses its intranet to share homework and timetables with students.
= 那所学校用内部网络与学生分享作业和课程表。
an intranet = 内部网络

intransigent
/ɪnˈtrænsɪdʒənt/
核心：（正式，贬）不妥协的、固执的 —— 坚持立场、拒不让步。名词 intransigence 并入本条。
① The union accused management of being intransigent over pay.
= 工会指责资方在工资问题上毫不让步。
be intransigent over something = 在…上毫不让步
② The talks failed because of the intransigence of both sides.
= 由于双方都不肯让步，谈判失败了。
the intransigence of somebody = 某人的不妥协

intransitive
/ɪnˈtrænsɪtɪv/
核心：（语法）不及物的 —— 动词后面不接宾语（sleep、arrive）。副词 intransitively 并入本条。
① Dictionaries mark intransitive verbs so that learners know they take no object.
= 词典会标出不及物动词，让学习者知道它们不带宾语。
an intransitive verb = 不及物动词
② Many verbs, such as open and break, can be used both transitively and intransitively.
= 许多动词，比如「open」和「break」，既可及物也可不及物地使用。
intransitively = 不及物地

intrastate
/ˌɪntrəˈsteɪt/
核心：（美）州内的 —— 在同一个州之内的（贸易、交通），跟 interstate 相对。
① Intrastate flights are cheaper because they are not taxed in the same way.
= 州内航班更便宜，因为它们的征税方式不同。
intrastate flights = 州内航班
② The law applies only to intrastate trade, not to goods sent to other states.
= 那项法律只适用于州内贸易，不适用于运往其他州的货物。
intrastate trade = 州内贸易

intrauterine
/ˌɪntrəˈjuːtəraɪn/
核心：（医学）子宫内的 —— intrauterine device（宫内节育器，缩写「IUD」）并入本条。
① Doctors monitor the baby's intrauterine growth with regular scans.
= 医生通过定期扫描监测胎儿在子宫内的生长情况。
intrauterine growth = 宫内生长
② She had an intrauterine device fitted after the birth of her second child.
= 生了第二个孩子后，她上了一个宫内节育器。
an intrauterine device = 宫内节育器

intravenous
/ˌɪntrəˈviːnəs/
核心：静脉内的、静脉注射的 —— 说输液、注射。副词 intravenously 并入本条。
① The patient was given intravenous fluids because he could not drink.
= 病人喝不了水，所以给他静脉输液。
intravenous fluids = 静脉输液
② The antibiotic is given intravenously every eight hours.
= 那种抗生素每八小时静脉注射一次。
intravenously = 经静脉地

intrepid
/ɪnˈtrepɪd/
核心：（常谑）无畏的、勇敢的 —— 多说探险家、旅行者，常带点玩笑。
① The intrepid explorers crossed the desert on foot with only two camels.
= 那几位无畏的探险家只带着两头骆驼徒步穿越了沙漠。
intrepid explorers = 无畏的探险家
② A few intrepid swimmers went into the sea on New Year's Day.
= 元旦那天，有几个勇敢的泳者下海游泳了。
intrepid swimmers = 勇敢的泳者
带调侃：做别人觉得有点傻的冒险事。

intricate
/ˈɪntrɪkət/
核心：错综复杂的、精细的 —— 由许多小部分精巧地组合而成。名词 intricacy 与副词 intricately 并入本条。
① The old carpet has an intricate pattern of birds and flowers.
= 那张旧地毯上有鸟和花组成的精细图案。
an intricate pattern = 精细的图案
② Few people understand the intricacies of the tax system.
= 很少有人懂得税制的复杂细节。
an intricacy = 复杂之处
多用复数：the intricacies of something（…的复杂细节）。
③ The box is intricately carved with scenes from the life of the saint.
= 那个盒子上精雕细刻着那位圣徒一生的场景。
intricately carved = 精雕细刻的

intrigue
/ɪnˈtriːɡ/（动）/ˈɪntriːɡ/（名）
核心：（使）好奇、引起兴趣；阴谋、密谋。动词（重音在后）：让人很想知道（be intrigued by）；
名词（重音在前）：秘密的策划、勾心斗角（political intrigue）。
形容词 intrigued（好奇的）、intriguing（引人入胜的）与副词 intriguingly 并入本条。
① I was intrigued by her story about the letters she found in the attic.
= 她说在阁楼上找到那些信的事，让我非常好奇。
be intrigued by something = 对…感到好奇
② The novel is full of political intrigue at the royal court.
= 那部小说满是宫廷里的政治阴谋。
political intrigue = 政治阴谋
③ It is an intriguing question that scientists have not yet answered.
= 这是个引人好奇、科学家尚未解答的问题。
an intriguing question = 引人好奇的问题
④ Intriguingly, the letter was signed with a different name.
= 耐人寻味的是，那封信署的是另一个名字。
intriguingly = 耐人寻味的是
⑤ He intrigued with the king's enemies to seize the throne.
= 他勾结国王的敌人，密谋夺取王位。
intrigue with somebody = 与某人密谋
动词的这一支偏旧，多见于历史叙述。

intrinsic
/ɪnˈtrɪnsɪk/
核心：内在的、固有的 —— 本身就有、不依赖外部的。常见 intrinsic value、intrinsic to。副词 intrinsically 并入本条。
① The ring has little intrinsic value, but it means a lot to her.
= 那枚戒指本身不值钱，但对她意义重大。
intrinsic value = 内在价值
② Music is intrinsic to the culture of the island.
= 音乐是那座岛上文化的固有部分。
be intrinsic to something = 是…所固有的
③ There is nothing intrinsically wrong with borrowing money.
= 借钱本身并没有错。
intrinsically = 本质上

intro
/ˈɪntrəʊ/
核心：（口语）开场白、前奏；介绍 —— introduction 的截短，多说歌曲的前奏、节目的开头，也说把人介绍给别人。
① The song has a long guitar intro before the singing starts.
= 那首歌在开唱前有一段很长的吉他前奏。
a guitar intro = 吉他前奏
② Can you give me an intro to your friend who works in publishing?
= 你能把我介绍给你那个做出版的朋友吗？
an intro to somebody = 对某人的引荐

introduce
/ˌɪntrəˈdjuːs/
核心：介绍、引见；引进、推行；引入、开始讲；主持。几支：让两人认识（introduce A to B）；
第一次把新东西带进来使用（introduce a new law / a species）；把人引向某种经历（introduce somebody to jazz）；
节目、演讲开头的介绍。名词 introduction 另立。
① Let me introduce you to my sister, who has just moved here from Canada.
= 我来介绍一下我妹妹，她刚从加拿大搬来。
introduce A to B = 把A介绍给B
② On the first day each student stood up to introduce themselves to the class.
= 第一天，每个学生都站起来向全班作自我介绍。
introduce yourself = 自我介绍
introduce oneself = 自我介绍（正式写法）
③ The government plans to introduce a new tax on sugary drinks.
= 政府计划对含糖饮料征收一种新税。
introduce a tax = 开征新税
④ Rabbits were introduced into Australia in the nineteenth century.
= 兔子是十九世纪被引进澳大利亚的。
introduce something into somewhere = 把…引进某地
⑤ Her father introduced her to jazz when she was only six.
= 她父亲在她六岁时就带她领略了爵士乐。
introduce somebody to something = 让某人初次接触…
⑥ The host introduced the programme with a short song.
= 主持人用一首短歌开始了节目。
introduce a programme = 介绍节目、开场

introduction
/ˌɪntrəˈdʌkʃən/
核心：介绍、引见；引进、推行；导言、序言；入门。几支：把人介绍给别人（make the introductions）；
新事物的首次使用（the introduction of the euro）；书、演讲的开头部分；入门读物（an introduction to）。
① She made the introductions and then left us to talk.
= 她给我们互相作了介绍，然后让我们自己聊。
make the introductions = 作介绍
② The introduction of the new system caused months of confusion.
= 新系统的推行造成了几个月的混乱。
the introduction of something = …的推行
③ In the introduction, the author explains why she wrote the book.
= 作者在序言里解释了她为什么写这本书。
the introduction = 序言、导言
④ This book is a good introduction to the history of art.
= 这本书是艺术史的一本很好的入门读物。
an introduction to something = …入门

introductory
/ˌɪntrəˈdʌktəri/
核心：介绍性的、入门的；开场的 —— 说课程、讲话、优惠。
① She is teaching an introductory course in psychology.
= 她在教一门心理学入门课。
an introductory course = 入门课程
② The magazine is available at a special introductory price of one pound.
= 那本杂志以一英镑的特价试售。
an introductory price = 试销价
③ After a few introductory remarks, the speaker turned to the main subject.
= 讲了几句开场白之后，演讲者转入了正题。
introductory remarks = 开场白

introspection
/ˌɪntrəˈspekʃən/
核心：内省、反省 —— 审视自己的想法和感受。不可数。
① Long walks alone gave him time for introspection.
= 独自长途散步让他有时间反省自己。
time for introspection = 反省的时间
② After the defeat, the party went through a period of painful introspection.
= 败选后，那个党经历了一段痛苦的自我反省。
a period of introspection = 一段反省期

introspective
/ˌɪntrəˈspektɪv/
核心：内省的、好反省的 —— 说人爱审视自己的内心，也说作品。
① She became quiet and introspective after her father died.
= 父亲去世后，她变得沉默而爱反省。
become introspective = 变得爱反省
② The album is more introspective than their earlier records.
= 那张专辑比他们早期的唱片更内省。
an introspective album = 内省的专辑

introvert
/ˈɪntrəvɜːt/
核心：内向的人 —— 安静、喜欢独处、在人多时容易疲惫的人。反义 extrovert。
名词 introversion（内向）与形容词 introverted（内向的）并入本条。
① As an introvert, she prefers quiet evenings at home to big parties.
= 作为一个内向的人，她更喜欢在家安静地过夜晚，而不是参加大聚会。
an introvert = 内向的人
② He is quiet and introverted, but he is very funny once you know him.
= 他安静内向，可你一旦跟他熟了，就会发现他很风趣。
introverted = 内向的
③ Psychologists study introversion and its effect on how people work.
= 心理学家研究内向性格及其对人们工作方式的影响。
introversion = 内向

intrude
/ɪnˈtruːd/
核心：闯入、侵入；打扰 —— 不受欢迎地进入某处或介入某事。常见 intrude on/into。
① I'm sorry to intrude, but I need to speak to your father urgently.
= 抱歉打扰了，可我有急事要跟你父亲说。
sorry to intrude = 抱歉打扰
② The press should not intrude into the private lives of ordinary people.
= 媒体不应侵扰普通人的私生活。
intrude into something = 侵扰…
③ Work increasingly intrudes on family time because of mobile phones.
= 因为手机，工作越来越多地侵占家庭时间。
intrude on something = 侵占…

intruder
/ɪnˈtruːdə(r)/
核心：闯入者、入侵者 —— 未经允许进入某地的人，常指潜入住宅的窃贼。
① The alarm went off when an intruder broke into the house at night.
= 夜里有人闯进房子，警报响了。
an intruder = 闯入者
② The guests at the private party treated him as an intruder.
= 私人聚会上的客人们把他当作不速之客。
treat somebody as an intruder = 把某人当作不速之客

intrusion
/ɪnˈtruːʒən/
核心：闯入、侵扰；干扰 —— 不受欢迎地进入或介入。可数不可数都用。
① She saw the reporters at her door as an intrusion into her grief.
= 她觉得记者找上门来是对她哀痛的侵扰。
an intrusion into something = 对…的侵扰
② Many people object to the intrusion of cameras into every public place.
= 许多人反对摄像头侵入每个公共场所。
the intrusion of something = …的侵入

intrusive
/ɪnˈtruːsɪv/
核心：侵扰的、打扰人的 —— 让人觉得私人空间被侵犯。
① I found his questions about my salary rather intrusive.
= 我觉得他问我工资的那些问题相当冒昧。
intrusive questions = 冒昧的问题
② The new motorway is an intrusive presence in the quiet valley.
= 新建的高速公路横在那个宁静的山谷里，显得很扎眼。
an intrusive presence = 碍眼的存在

intubate
/ˈɪntjʊbeɪt/
核心：（医学）插管 —— 把管子插进病人的气管，帮助呼吸。
① The paramedics had to intubate the patient before taking him to hospital.
= 急救人员在送病人去医院之前，不得不给他插了管。
intubate a patient = 给病人插管
② Patients who are intubated cannot speak until the tube is removed.
= 插了管的病人在管子拔掉之前说不了话。
be intubated = 被插管

intuit
/ɪnˈtjuːɪt/
核心：（正式）凭直觉知道、直觉感知 —— 不经推理就明白。
① She intuited that something was wrong from the tone of his voice.
= 从他的语气里，她直觉地感到出事了。
intuit that = 凭直觉感到…
② Good teachers can often intuit what a shy child needs.
= 好老师常能凭直觉知道一个害羞的孩子需要什么。
intuit something = 直觉地感知…

intuition
/ˌɪntjuˈɪʃən/
核心：直觉；直觉感知的事 —— 不经推理、凭感觉就知道的能力。可数时指一个具体的直觉判断。
① My intuition told me not to trust the man who was selling the car.
= 我的直觉告诉我，别相信那个卖车的人。
somebody's intuition = 某人的直觉
② She had an intuition that the phone call would bring bad news.
= 她有种直觉，那个电话会带来坏消息。
have an intuition that = 有种直觉…

intuitive
/ˌɪnˈtjuːˈɪtɪv/
核心：直觉的；（设计）易懂好用的。两支：凭直觉的、有直觉力的（an intuitive understanding）；
软件、界面不用学就会用（an intuitive interface）。副词 intuitively 并入本条。
① She has an intuitive understanding of how children think.
= 她对孩子怎么想有一种直觉上的理解。
an intuitive understanding = 直觉上的理解
② The new phone is so intuitive that my grandmother learned to use it in a day.
= 新手机简单易用，我奶奶一天就学会了。
intuitive = 易懂好用的
③ He knew intuitively that the plan would fail.
= 他凭直觉就知道那个计划会失败。
intuitively = 凭直觉地

Inuit
/ˈɪnjuɪt/
核心：因纽特人 —— 生活在北极地区（加拿大、格陵兰、阿拉斯加）的原住民；也作形容词。
许多因纽特人不愿被称为 Eskimo，Inuit 是今天通用的称呼。
① Many Inuit still hunt seals and fish through holes in the ice.
= 许多因纽特人至今仍在冰上凿洞捕海豹、捕鱼。
the Inuit = 因纽特人
② The museum has a large collection of Inuit art and carvings.
= 那家博物馆收藏了大量因纽特艺术品和雕刻。
Inuit art = 因纽特艺术

Inuktitut
/ɪˈnʊktɪtʊt/
核心：因纽特语 —— 加拿大东部因纽特人的语言，在努纳武特地区是官方语言之一。
① Road signs in the town are written in both Inuktitut and English.
= 那个镇上的路标用因纽特语和英语双语书写。
Inuktitut = 因纽特语
② Children in the region now learn Inuktitut at school.
= 那个地区的孩子们现在在学校学因纽特语。
learn Inuktitut = 学因纽特语

inundate
/ˈɪnʌndeɪt/
核心：淹没；使应接不暇 —— 本义是洪水淹没；比喻大量的信件、请求像潮水般涌来（be inundated with）。
名词 inundation 并入本条。
① After the TV programme, the charity was inundated with offers of help.
= 电视节目播出后，那家慈善机构收到了潮水般的援助提议。
be inundated with something = 被…淹没、应接不暇
② The river burst its banks and inundated the fields for miles around.
= 河水决堤，淹没了方圆数英里的田地。
inundate something = 淹没…
③ The whole valley was lost to inundation when the dam was built.
= 水坝建成后，整个山谷被淹没了。
inundation = 淹没

inure
/ɪˈnjʊə(r)/
核心：（正式）使习惯于（困难、痛苦）—— 多用被动 be inured to something：已经习惯到不再觉得难受。
inure to 并入本条。
① Years of living in the city had inured her to the noise of the traffic.
= 多年城市生活让她对车流噪音已经习以为常。
inure somebody to something = 使某人习惯于…
② Nurses become inured to the sight of blood.
= 护士们对见血已经习以为常。
be inured to something = 对…习以为常

invade
/ɪnˈveɪd/
核心：侵略、侵入；涌入；侵犯。几支：军队进入别国领土（invade a country）；
大批人涌进某地（fans invaded the pitch）；侵扰（隐私）；疾病、细胞侵入身体。侵略者 invader 并入本条。
① The army invaded the country from the north in the spring of 1940.
= 一九四〇年春天，那支军队从北面入侵了那个国家。
invade a country = 入侵一个国家
② Hundreds of fans invaded the pitch after the final whistle.
= 终场哨响后，成百上千的球迷冲进了球场。
invade the pitch = 冲进球场
③ The photographers invaded her privacy by following her on holiday.
= 摄影记者一路跟着她去度假，侵犯了她的隐私。
invade somebody's privacy = 侵犯某人的隐私
④ The castle was built to defend the town against invaders from the sea.
= 那座城堡是为了抵御从海上来的侵略者而建的。
an invader = 侵略者

invalid
/ɪnˈvælɪd/（无效的）/ˈɪnvəlɪd/（病弱者）
核心：两个词同形。形容词（重音在后）：无效的、作废的（an invalid passport）；
（论点）站不住脚的。名词（重音在前）：（旧，现多嫌冒犯）病弱者、残疾人。
名词 invalidity（无效；（英）残疾）并入本条。
① Your ticket is invalid because it is for yesterday's train.
= 你的票无效，因为那是昨天那班车的。
an invalid ticket = 无效车票
② The court declared the election result invalid.
= 法院宣布选举结果无效。
declare something invalid = 宣布…无效
③ She spent twenty years caring for her father, who was an invalid.
= 她花了二十年照顾病弱的父亲。
an invalid = 病弱者（旧）
今天多说 a person with a disability 或 a sick person。
④ The lawyer argued for the invalidity of the contract.
= 律师论证那份合同无效。
the invalidity of something = …的无效

invalidate
/ɪnˈvælɪdeɪt/
核心：使无效、使作废；证明（论点）站不住脚。名词 invalidation 并入本条。
① Any handwritten change to the signed document will invalidate it in the eyes of the court.
= 对签过字的文件做任何手写改动，在法庭看来都会使它失效。
invalidate something = 使…无效
② New evidence from the ancient bones invalidated the old theory about the first farmers.
= 那些古骨提供的新证据，推翻了关于最早农民的旧理论。
invalidate a theory = 推翻一个理论
③ The invalidation of the election result by the court led to weeks of angry protests.
= 法院宣布选举结果无效，引发了几个星期的愤怒抗议。
the invalidation of something = …的作废

invaluable
/ɪnˈvæljʊbəl/
核心：极其宝贵的、无价的 —— 注意不是 valuable 的反面，而是「贵重得无法估价」。
① Her experience of working abroad proved invaluable when the company expanded.
= 公司扩张时，她在国外工作的经验证明极其宝贵。
prove invaluable = 证明极有价值
② The internet is an invaluable source of information for students.
= 互联网对学生来说是极其宝贵的信息来源。
an invaluable source = 极宝贵的来源

invariable
/ɪnˈveəriəbəl/
核心：不变的、始终如一的 —— 从不改变的。副词 invariably（总是、一贯）最常用，并入本条。
① Her invariable answer to every question was "Ask your father."
= 无论问她什么，她的回答总是「去问你爸爸」。
an invariable answer = 一成不变的回答
② Whatever the weather, my uncle invariably arrives late for family dinners and leaves early.
= 不管天气怎样，我叔叔参加家宴总是迟到早退。
invariably = 总是、一贯

invariant
/ɪnˈveəriənt/
核心：（数学、科学）不变的；不变量 —— 在变换中保持不变的量或性质。
① The speed of light is invariant, whatever the speed of the observer.
= 无论观察者速度如何，光速都是不变的。
be invariant = 保持不变
② Mathematicians look for invariants that stay the same when a shape is stretched.
= 数学家寻找在图形被拉伸时保持不变的量。
an invariant = 不变量

invasion
/ɪnˈveɪʒən/
核心：侵略、入侵；涌入；侵犯。invade 的名词，几支对应：军事入侵（the invasion of）；
大批涌入（an invasion of tourists）；侵犯（an invasion of privacy）。
① The invasion began at dawn with an attack on the coast.
= 入侵在黎明时分以对海岸的攻击开始。
an invasion = 入侵
② Every summer the village suffers an invasion of tourists.
= 每年夏天，那个村子都会遭到游客的大举涌入。
an invasion of tourists = 游客的涌入
③ Reading someone's diary is an invasion of privacy.
= 看别人的日记是侵犯隐私。
an invasion of privacy = 侵犯隐私

invasive
/ɪnˈveɪsɪv/
核心：侵入的；（医学）侵入性的、创伤性的；（物种）入侵的。几支：
医学上需要切开身体的（invasive surgery）；疾病扩散的；外来物种泛滥成灾的（invasive species）。
① The new treatment is less invasive than traditional surgery.
= 新疗法的创伤比传统手术小。
invasive surgery = 侵入性手术
② Invasive plants from other countries are crowding out native species.
= 来自别国的入侵植物正在排挤本地物种。
invasive species = 入侵物种
③ Many people find the new security checks invasive.
= 许多人觉得新的安检措施侵扰隐私。
invasive = 侵扰的
④ A non-invasive scan can detect the blockage without any need for surgery.
= 一次无创的扫描就能查出堵塞，不必动手术。
non-invasive = 无创的

invective
/ɪnˈvektɪv/
核心：（正式）痛骂、抨击、谩骂 —— 不可数，指一连串激烈的辱骂言辞。
① The politician let loose a stream of invective against his opponents.
= 那位政客对他的对手们发出了一连串的抨击。
a stream of invective = 一连串的谩骂
② The article is full of personal invective and contains few facts.
= 那篇文章满是人身攻击，却没几条事实。
personal invective = 人身攻击

inveigh
/ɪnˈveɪ/
核心：（正式）痛斥、猛烈抨击 —— 几乎只用 inveigh against something。inveigh against 并入本条。
① The preacher inveighed against the evils of gambling.
= 传教士痛斥赌博之恶。
inveigh against something = 痛斥…
② Critics inveighed against the new law as an attack on free speech.
= 批评者猛烈抨击那项新法律，称其是对言论自由的攻击。
inveigh against a law = 抨击一项法律

inveigle
/ɪnˈveɪɡəl/
核心：（正式）哄骗、诱使 —— 用花言巧语让人做某事或得到某物（inveigle somebody into doing）。
① He inveigled his aunt into lending him money for a business that never existed.
= 他哄骗姑妈借钱给他，去做一桩根本不存在的生意。
inveigle somebody into doing something = 哄骗某人做…
② She inveigled her way into the director's office by pretending to be a journalist.
= 她假装记者，混进了董事的办公室。
inveigle your way into somewhere = 设法混进某处

invent
/ɪnˈvent/
核心：发明；编造、捏造。两支：创造出以前没有的东西（invent a machine）；
编出假的故事、借口（invent an excuse）。名词 invention、inventor 另立。
① Alexander Graham Bell is usually said to have invented the telephone.
= 人们通常说是贝尔发明了电话。
invent something = 发明…
② He invented an excuse about a sick grandmother to leave work early.
= 他编了个奶奶生病的借口，提前下了班。
invent an excuse = 编造借口

invention
/ɪnˈvenʃən/
核心：发明；发明物；编造；创造力。几支：发明这件事（the invention of printing）；一项具体的发明（a clever invention）；
虚构的故事（pure invention）；创造性。
① The invention of the printing press changed the world.
= 印刷机的发明改变了世界。
the invention of something = …的发明
② His latest invention is a bicycle that folds up into a small bag.
= 他最新的发明是一辆可以折进小包里的自行车。
an invention = 发明物
③ The story about his time in the army was pure invention.
= 他那些当兵的故事纯属编造。
pure invention = 纯属编造

inventive
/ɪnˈventɪv/
核心：有创造力的、善于发明的；新颖的。副词 inventively 与名词 inventiveness 并入本条。
① She is an inventive cook who never follows a recipe exactly.
= 她是个很有创意的厨师，从不照搬食谱。
an inventive cook = 有创意的厨师
② The old warehouse has been inventively turned into a theatre.
= 那座旧仓库被别出心裁地改成了剧院。
inventively = 别出心裁地
③ Children often show great inventiveness in their games.
= 孩子们在游戏中常常表现出很强的创造力。
inventiveness = 创造力

inventor
/ɪnˈventə(r)/
核心：发明者、发明家 —— 发明了某种东西的人。
① The inventor of the washing machine in the museum never made any money from it.
= 博物馆里那台洗衣机的发明者从来没靠它赚过钱。
the inventor of something = …的发明者
② As a child she wanted to be an inventor and filled the garage with strange machines.
= 她小时候想当发明家，把车库塞满了奇怪的机器。
an inventor = 发明家

inventory
/ˈɪnvəntəri/
核心：清单、存货清单；存货。两支：一份详细列出物品的清单（make an inventory）；
（美）店里、仓库里的全部存货（英式多说 stock）。
① The landlord made an inventory of all the furniture before we moved in.
= 我们搬进去之前，房东把所有家具列了一份清单。
make an inventory of something = 列出…的清单
② The shop is selling off its old inventory at half price.
= 那家店正在半价清仓旧存货。
inventory = （美）存货

inverse
/ˌɪnˈvɜːs/
核心：相反的、反向的；反面、逆 —— 数学上指反比（in inverse proportion）、逆运算；一般说正好倒过来的关系。
副词 inversely 并入本条。
① The number of mistakes rose in inverse proportion to the time the students were given.
= 给学生的时间越少，错误就越多，二者成反比。
in inverse proportion to something = 与…成反比
② Adding is the inverse of subtracting, so one can undo the other.
= 加法是减法的逆运算，所以一个能抵消另一个。
the inverse of something = …的逆、反面
③ The price of the old bonds moves inversely to interest rates.
= 那些旧债券的价格与利率反向变动。
inversely = 相反地、成反比地

inversion
/ɪnˈvɜːʒən/
核心：倒置、颠倒；（语法）倒装；（气象）逆温。本义是把顺序、位置倒过来。
① The inversion of the usual roles meant that the children cooked dinner for their parents.
= 角色一颠倒，就成了孩子们给父母做晚饭。
the inversion of something = …的颠倒
② In questions such as "Are you ready?", English uses inversion of the subject and the verb.
= 在「Are you ready?」这类问句里，英语把主语和动词倒装。
inversion = 倒装
③ A temperature inversion trapped the smoke over the city for three days.
= 逆温现象把烟雾困在城市上空三天。
a temperature inversion = 逆温

invert
/ɪnˈvɜːt/
核心：倒置、颠倒 —— 把东西上下或前后翻过来。形容词 inverted（倒置的）并入本条；
inverted commas（英，引号）与 inverted snobbery（反向势利，看不起上层的东西以显示自己接地气）也并在这里。
① Invert the cake onto a plate as soon as it comes out of the oven.
= 蛋糕一出炉就把它倒扣在盘子上。
invert something = 把…倒过来
② The picture in the camera is inverted, so the photographer sees everything upside down.
= 相机里的图像是倒过来的，所以摄影师看到的一切都是颠倒的。
inverted = 倒置的
③ Put the title of the poem in inverted commas.
= 把诗的题目放在引号里。
inverted commas = （英）引号
口语里也说 in inverted commas，表示「所谓的」。
④ His refusal to eat in expensive restaurants is a kind of inverted snobbery.
= 他拒绝去高档餐馆吃饭，是一种反向势利。
inverted snobbery = 反向势利

invertebrate
/ɪnˈvɜːtɪbrət/
核心：无脊椎动物 —— 没有脊骨的动物，如虫、蜗牛、水母。也作形容词。
① Most of the animals living in the pond are invertebrates such as snails and insects.
= 池塘里的动物大多是蜗牛、昆虫之类的无脊椎动物。
an invertebrate = 无脊椎动物
② Scientists counted over two hundred invertebrate species in a single tree.
= 科学家在一棵树上就数出了两百多种无脊椎动物。
invertebrate species = 无脊椎动物物种

invest
/ɪnˈvest/
核心：投资；投入（时间、精力）；（正式）授予。几支：把钱放进能生利的地方（invest in shares）；
为得到回报而花时间精力（invest time in）；给人正式授予权力、称号（invest somebody with）。
invest in、invest with 并入本条；名词 investment、investor 另立。
① She invested all her savings in a small restaurant.
= 她把全部积蓄投资在一家小餐馆上。
invest in something = 投资于…
② The government plans to invest heavily in public transport.
= 政府计划在公共交通上大量投资。
invest heavily = 大量投资
③ We've invested a lot of time in this project, so we don't want it to fail.
= 我们在这个项目上投入了大量时间，所以不想让它失败。
invest time in something = 在…上投入时间
④ Why don't you invest in a new coat? That one is falling apart.
= 你为什么不买件新外套？那件都快散架了。
invest in something = （口语，谑）花钱买…
⑤ The new constitution invests the president with the power to dismiss the government.
= 新宪法赋予总统解散政府的权力。
invest somebody with something = 授予某人…

investigate
/ɪnˈvestɪɡeɪt/
核心：调查、研究 —— 仔细查明事实真相，多说警方、官方、科学研究。
① Police are investigating the death of a man found in the river.
= 警方正在调查河里发现的一具男尸的死因。
investigate a death = 调查死因
② Scientists are investigating whether the drug can slow down memory loss.
= 科学家正在研究这种药能否减缓记忆衰退。
investigate whether = 研究是否…
③ I heard a noise downstairs and went to investigate.
= 我听到楼下有响声，就下去看看是怎么回事。
go to investigate = 去看个究竟
不及物，口语里指去查看一下。

investigation
/ɪnˌvestɪˈɡeɪʃən/
核心：调查、研究 —— 正式、系统地查明事实。常见 under investigation（在调查中）、an investigation into。
① The police have launched an investigation into the robbery.
= 警方已就这起抢劫案展开调查。
an investigation into something = 对…的调查
② Two officials are under investigation for taking bribes.
= 两名官员因受贿正在接受调查。
be under investigation = 在接受调查
③ Scientific investigation has shown that the river is badly polluted.
= 科学研究表明那条河污染严重。
scientific investigation = 科学研究

investigative
/ɪnˈvestɪɡətɪv/
核心：调查的、探究的 —— 多说新闻报道（investigative journalism，调查性新闻）。
① She is an investigative journalist who spent two years exposing the fraud.
= 她是一名调查记者，花了两年时间揭露那起诈骗。
an investigative journalist = 调查记者
② The police have wide investigative powers under the new law.
= 根据新法律，警方拥有广泛的调查权。
investigative powers = 调查权

investigator
/ɪnˈvestɪɡeɪtə(r)/
核心：调查者、调查员 —— 调查事故、罪案的人；private investigator 是私家侦探。
① Accident investigators examined the wreck of the plane for weeks.
= 事故调查员花了几个星期检查飞机残骸。
an accident investigator = 事故调查员
② She hired a private investigator to find out where her husband went every Friday.
= 她雇了一名私家侦探，查清丈夫每周五去了哪里。
a private investigator = 私家侦探

investiture
/ɪnˈvestɪtʃə(r)/
核心：授职仪式、授衔典礼 —— 正式授予某人官职、爵位、荣誉的典礼。
① The investiture took place at the palace in front of the prince's family.
= 授衔典礼在王宫里举行，王子的家人在场观礼。
an investiture = 授衔典礼
② She received her medal at an investiture ceremony in June.
= 她在六月的一次授勋仪式上领取了勋章。
an investiture ceremony = 授勋仪式

investment
/ɪnˈvestmənt/
核心：投资；投资额；投资物；（时间精力的）投入。可数不可数都用。
investment bank（投资银行）、investment banker（投资银行家）、investment banking（投资银行业务）并入本条。
① The country needs more foreign investment to create jobs.
= 那个国家需要更多外国投资来创造就业。
foreign investment = 外国投资
② Buying the flat was the best investment he ever made.
= 买那套公寓是他做过的最好的投资。
an investment = 一项投资
③ Learning a language is a big investment of time and effort.
= 学一门语言需要投入大量的时间和精力。
an investment of time = 时间的投入
④ He worked for an investment bank in London for ten years.
= 他在伦敦一家投资银行工作了十年。
an investment bank = 投资银行
⑤ As an investment banker, she advised companies on mergers.
= 作为一名投资银行家，她为企业的合并提供咨询。
an investment banker = 投资银行家
⑥ Investment banking is famous for long hours and huge bonuses.
= 投资银行业以工作时间长、奖金高而出名。
investment banking = 投资银行业务

investor
/ɪnˈvestə(r)/
核心：投资者 —— 把钱投进企业、股票、房产的人或机构。
① Small investors lost millions when the building company collapsed without warning.
= 那家建筑公司毫无预兆地倒闭，小投资者损失了数百万。
investors = 投资者
② The business is looking for an investor to help it open new shops.
= 那家企业正在寻找一位投资者，帮它开新店。
an investor = 投资者

inveterate
/ɪnˈvetərət/
核心：（贬或谑）积习难改的、根深蒂固的 —— 只放在名词前：an inveterate liar / gambler。
① He is an inveterate liar, so don't believe a word he says.
= 他是个撒谎成性的人，他的话一个字也别信。
an inveterate liar = 撒谎成性的人
② My grandfather was an inveterate traveller who visited sixty countries.
= 我祖父是个旅行成瘾的人，去过六十个国家。
an inveterate traveller = 旅行成瘾的人
谑用，不一定是坏习惯。

invidious
/ɪnˈvɪdiəs/
核心：（正式）招人怨恨的、得罪人的；不公平的。多说让人处于尴尬境地的比较或选择。
① It would be invidious to single out one member of the team for praise.
= 单独表扬团队里的某个人会招人怨。
it would be invidious to do something = 做…会得罪人
② Teachers were put in the invidious position of choosing which pupils could go on the trip.
= 老师们被置于两难的境地，要挑选哪些学生可以去旅行。
an invidious position = 招人怨恨的处境

invigilate
/ɪnˈvɪdʒɪleɪt/
核心：（英）监考 —— 在考场监督考生，防止作弊。名词 invigilation 与监考人 invigilator 并入本条。美式说 proctor。
① Two teachers invigilate each exam in the main hall.
= 每场考试由两位老师在大厅监考。
invigilate an exam = 监考
② Invigilation is one of the least popular jobs in the school.
= 监考是学校里最不受欢迎的工作之一。
invigilation = 监考
③ The invigilator told us to put our pens down.
= 监考老师让我们放下笔。
an invigilator = 监考人

invigorate
/ɪnˈvɪɡəreɪt/
核心：使精力充沛、使振作；使活跃。本义让人觉得有力气、有精神；比喻给经济、组织注入活力。
形容词 invigorating（令人精神焕发的）并入本条。
① A cold shower and a strong coffee in the morning always invigorate me before work.
= 早上上班前冲个冷水澡、喝杯浓咖啡，总能让我精神焕发。
invigorate somebody = 使某人精神焕发
② In less than a year, the young manager has invigorated the whole company with fresh ideas.
= 不到一年，那位年轻的经理就用新想法给整个公司注入了活力。
invigorate a company = 使公司充满活力
③ We went for an invigorating walk along the cliffs.
= 我们沿着悬崖散了一次让人精神一振的步。
an invigorating walk = 令人精神一振的散步

invincible
/ɪnˈvɪnsəbəl/
核心：不可战胜的、无敌的 —— 强大到打不败。名词 invincibility 并入本条。
① The team seemed invincible after winning twenty games in a row.
= 连赢二十场之后，那支球队似乎所向无敌。
seem invincible = 似乎无敌
② Young drivers often have a feeling of invincibility that leads to accidents.
= 年轻司机常有一种自己无所不能的感觉，这容易导致事故。
a feeling of invincibility = 无敌的感觉

inviolable
/ɪnˈvaɪələbəl/
核心：（正式）不可侵犯的、不容违背的 —— 说权利、规则、边界、承诺。名词 inviolability 并入本条。
① The first article of the constitution declares that human dignity is inviolable.
= 宪法第一条宣布人的尊严不可侵犯。
be inviolable = 不可侵犯
② The peace treaty signed after the war guaranteed the inviolability of the border.
= 战后签订的和平条约保证了边界不可侵犯。
the inviolability of something = …的不可侵犯

inviolate
/ɪnˈvaɪələt/
核心：（正式）未受侵犯的、完好无损的 —— 保持原样、没有被破坏。
① Despite the war, the old library remained inviolate.
= 尽管经历了战争，那座古老的图书馆依然完好无损。
remain inviolate = 保持完好
② He believed that the privacy of letters should be inviolate.
= 他认为信件的隐私应当不受侵犯。
be inviolate = 不受侵犯

invisible
/ɪnˈvɪzɪbəl/
核心：看不见的、隐形的；无形的、不引人注意的。本义是眼睛看不到（invisible to the naked eye）；
比喻被忽视、不受重视的（feel invisible）；经济上指无形的（invisible earnings，服务业收入）。
名词 invisibility 与副词 invisibly 并入本条。
① Most of the bacteria on your kitchen table are invisible to the naked eye.
= 你厨房桌子上的细菌大多是肉眼看不见的。
invisible to the naked eye = 肉眼看不见的
② Many older women say they feel invisible in shops and restaurants.
= 许多上了年纪的女性说，她们在商店和餐馆里觉得自己像透明人一样。
feel invisible = 觉得被忽视
③ Tourism brings in large invisible earnings for the island.
= 旅游业为那座岛带来了大量无形收入。
invisible earnings = 无形收入
④ In the story, a magic cloak gives the boy the power of invisibility.
= 故事里，一件魔法斗篷让男孩拥有隐身的能力。
invisibility = 隐形
⑤ The two rooms are invisibly connected by a hidden door behind the bookcase.
= 两个房间由书柜后面的一扇暗门神不知鬼不觉地连着。
invisibly = 看不见地

invitation
/ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən/
核心：邀请；请柬；诱因。几支：请人来参加（an invitation to a party）；写着邀请的卡片；
（比喻）招来某事的做法（an invitation to thieves）。常见 at the invitation of（应…之邀）、by invitation only（凭请柬入场）。
① Thank you for your kind invitation to dinner.
= 谢谢你盛情邀请我吃晚饭。
an invitation to something = …的邀请
② The wedding invitations were sent out three months before the big day.
= 婚礼请柬在大喜日子前三个月就发出去了。
a wedding invitation = 婚礼请柬
③ She visited the university at the invitation of the professor.
= 她应那位教授之邀访问了那所大学。
at the invitation of somebody = 应某人之邀
④ Leaving your car unlocked is an open invitation to thieves.
= 不锁车门等于公开招贼。
an open invitation to somebody = 公开招引某人
⑤ Entry to the party is by invitation only.
= 聚会凭请柬入场。
by invitation only = 凭请柬入场

invitational
/ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃənəl/
核心：（美）邀请赛 —— 只有受邀者才能参加的比赛，也作形容词。
① She won the annual golf invitational at the country club.
= 她赢了乡村俱乐部一年一度的高尔夫邀请赛。
an invitational = 邀请赛
② Only the top twenty players are invited to the invitational tournament.
= 只有排名前二十的选手受邀参加这场邀请赛。
an invitational tournament = 邀请赛

invite
/ɪnˈvaɪt/（动）/ˈɪnvaɪt/（名）
核心：邀请；请求；招致。几支：请人来参加活动（invite somebody to/for）；正式请人做某事（invite applications）；
（行为）引来（不好的事）（invite trouble / criticism）。一串短语动词并入本条：
invite somebody back（请回来）、invite somebody along（请一起去）、invite somebody over / round / around（请到家里）、
invite somebody in（请进屋）。名词（口语）invite = 邀请。
① They invited us to their wedding in Italy.
= 他们邀请我们去参加在意大利举行的婚礼。
invite somebody to something = 邀请某人参加…
② Let's invite a few friends over for dinner on Saturday.
= 我们星期六请几个朋友到家里吃饭吧。
invite somebody over = 请某人到家里
这一组短语动词的宾语是代词时必须放中间（invite them over）；宾语是名词时也可放后面：
invite over the neighbours、invite round the whole class、invite around a few friends、
invite in the visitors、invite along a friend、invite back the old team。
③ My neighbours invited me round for coffee on my first day in the street.
= 我搬到这条街的第一天，邻居们就请我到他们家喝咖啡。
invite somebody round = （英）请某人到家里
invite somebody around = （美）请某人到家里
④ She opened the door and invited the police officers in.
= 她打开门，请警察们进来。
invite somebody in = 请某人进屋
⑤ We're going to the beach; why don't you invite your cousin along?
= 我们要去海滩，你何不请你表弟一起来？
invite somebody along = 请某人一起去
⑥ The hotel was so good that they invited us back for a free weekend.
= 那家酒店太好了，他们还请我们回去免费住一个周末。
invite somebody back = 请某人再来
⑦ The company is inviting applications for the post of manager.
= 公司正在招聘经理一职。
invite applications = 征求申请
⑧ Leaving your bag open in a crowd is just inviting trouble.
= 在人群里敞着包，简直是自找麻烦。
invite trouble = 招惹麻烦
⑨ Thanks for the invite, but I'm busy that night.
= 谢谢邀请，可那晚我有事。
an invite = （口语）邀请

inviting
/ɪnˈvaɪtɪŋ/
核心：诱人的、吸引人的 —— 让人想去、想做、想吃。副词 invitingly 并入本条。
① The clear blue water looked very inviting on such a hot day.
= 在这么热的天，清澈的蓝色海水看上去非常诱人。
look inviting = 看起来诱人
② The door of the bakery stood invitingly open, and the smell of bread filled the street.
= 面包店的门敞开着，很吸引人，面包的香味飘满了整条街。
invitingly = 诱人地

invocation
/ɪnvəˈkeɪʃən/
核心：（正式）祈求、祷告；援引 —— invoke 的名词。
① The ceremony began with an invocation to the gods of the harvest.
= 仪式以向丰收之神的祈祷开始。
an invocation to somebody = 向某人的祈求
② The minister's invocation of emergency powers was criticized by the courts.
= 部长援引紧急权力的做法受到了法院的批评。
the invocation of something = 对…的援引

invoice
/ˈɪnvɔɪs/
核心：发票、账单 —— 列明货物或服务及应付款项的单据。也作动词：给…开发票。
① Two weeks after the work was finished, the builder sent us an invoice for the new roof.
= 完工两周后，建筑商给我们寄来了新屋顶的账单。
an invoice for something = …的发票
② For regular customers, the printing company will invoice you at the end of each month.
= 对老客户，那家印刷公司会在每月月底开发票。
invoice somebody = 给某人开发票

invoke
/ɪnˈvəʊk/
核心：援引、行使（法律、权利）；提及（以支持观点）；祈求（神灵）；（计算机）调用。
几支：拿法律、规则做依据（invoke a law）；引用某人某事来支持自己（invoke the memory of）；
向神灵祈求帮助；唤起（某种感觉，同 evoke，这一用法有人认为不规范）。名词 invocation 另立。
① The government invoked emergency powers to deal with the floods.
= 政府动用紧急权力应对洪灾。
invoke powers = 动用权力
② He invoked the name of his famous father to get the job.
= 他搬出了他那位著名父亲的名字来得到这份工作。
invoke somebody's name = 搬出某人的名字
③ The priest invoked God's blessing on the new ship.
= 神父为那艘新船祈求上帝赐福。
invoke a blessing = 祈求赐福
④ The program invokes a separate function to print the results.
= 程序调用一个单独的函数来打印结果。
invoke a function = 调用函数

involuntary
/ɪnˈvɒləntəri/
核心：不由自主的、无意识的；非自愿的。两支：身体不受控制的反应（an involuntary cry）；
不是自己选择的（involuntary redundancy）。副词 involuntarily 并入本条。
① She gave an involuntary shiver when she walked into the cold church.
= 她走进冰冷的教堂时，不由自主地打了个寒战。
an involuntary shiver = 不由自主的寒战
② Hundreds of workers faced involuntary redundancy when the factory closed.
= 工厂关闭时，数百名工人被迫下岗。
involuntary redundancy = 非自愿裁员
③ He smiled involuntarily when he heard her voice.
= 听到她的声音，他不由自主地笑了。
involuntarily = 不由自主地

involve
/ɪnˈvɒlv/
核心：包含、涉及；使参与、牵涉。几支：一件事必然包括某部分（The job involves travelling）；
让人参与进来（involve somebody in）；把人牵连进（麻烦、罪行）。involve in 并入本条；
形容词 involved、名词 involvement 另立。
① The job involves a lot of travelling, so she is rarely at home.
= 那份工作需要经常出差，所以她很少在家。
involve doing something = 需要做…
后面接 -ing，不接不定式。
② Teachers try to involve all the children in the discussion.
= 老师们设法让所有孩子都参与讨论。
involve somebody in something = 使某人参与…
③ I don't want to involve you in my family's problems.
= 我不想把你牵扯进我家里的麻烦。
involve somebody in a problem = 把某人牵扯进麻烦
④ The accident involved three cars and a lorry.
= 那起事故涉及三辆汽车和一辆卡车。
involve something = 涉及…

involved
/ɪnˈvɒlvd/
核心：参与的、有关的；复杂的；（关系）亲密的。几支：卷入其中的（be involved in）；
过程、解释繁杂难懂（a long, involved story）；与某人有恋爱关系（be involved with somebody）；
付出很多时间精力（get involved）。
① Over a hundred people were involved in the rescue.
= 一百多人参与了营救。
be involved in something = 参与…
② She gets very involved in her work and forgets to eat.
= 她一投入工作就忘了吃饭。
get involved = 投入、参与
get involved in something = 参与…、卷入…
③ He told a long and involved story about why he was late.
= 他讲了个又长又绕的故事，说明自己为什么迟到。
an involved story = 复杂的故事
④ She is involved with a man she met on holiday.
= 她和一个度假时认识的男人好上了。
be involved with somebody = 与某人有恋爱关系

involvement
/ɪnˈvɒlvmənt/
核心：参与、介入；（恋爱）关系 —— involve 的名词。
① The police are investigating his involvement in the robbery.
= 警方正在调查他与那起抢劫案的牵连。
involvement in something = 参与…
② Research shows that parental involvement in primary schools helps children do better at reading.
= 研究表明，家长参与小学事务能帮助孩子提高阅读能力。
parental involvement = 家长参与
③ Her involvement with a married man shocked her family.
= 她和一个有妇之夫的关系让家人震惊。
an involvement with somebody = 与某人的关系

invulnerable
/ɪnˈvʌlnərəbəl/
核心：不会受伤害的、刀枪不入的；无懈可击的 —— 不可能被攻击、伤害或打败。名词 invulnerability 并入本条。
① In the legend, the hero is invulnerable except for one spot on his heel.
= 传说中，那位英雄除了脚后跟上的一处以外刀枪不入。
be invulnerable = 刀枪不入
② The party's huge majority makes it almost invulnerable at the next election.
= 那个党的巨大多数席位让它在下次选举中几乎立于不败之地。
almost invulnerable = 几乎无懈可击
③ Teenagers often have a sense of invulnerability that leads them to take risks.
= 青少年常有一种自己不会受伤的感觉，这让他们去冒险。
a sense of invulnerability = 自己不会受伤的感觉

inward
/ˈɪnwəd/
核心：内心的；向内的；输入的。几支：心里的（inward feelings）；朝里的（an inward curve）；
进入一国的（inward investment，外来投资）。也作副词，同 inwards。
副词 inwardly（在心里）与名词 inwardness（内在性、精神性）并入本条。
① She felt a sense of inward calm after making the decision.
= 做出决定后，她感到内心一片平静。
inward calm = 内心的平静
② The door opens inward, so stand back.
= 门是往里开的，往后站点。
open inward = 向内开
③ The government wants to attract more inward investment from abroad.
= 政府希望吸引更多外来投资。
inward investment = 外来投资
④ He smiled politely but inwardly he was furious.
= 他礼貌地笑着，心里却怒火中烧。
inwardly = 在心里
⑤ The poet writes about the inwardness of religious experience.
= 那位诗人写的是宗教体验的内在性。
inwardness = 内在性

inwards
/ˈɪnwədz/
核心：向内、向里 —— 副词，英式常用；美式多说 inward。
① The walls of the old barn were starting to lean inwards.
= 旧谷仓的墙开始往里歪了。
lean inwards = 向内倾斜
② The door swung inwards, and a cold wind blew into the hall.
= 门往里一荡，一股冷风灌进了门厅。
swing inwards = 向内摆动

iodide
/ˈaɪədaɪd/
核心：（化学）碘化物 —— 碘与另一种元素组成的化合物，如 potassium iodide（碘化钾）。
① People living near the power station were given potassium iodide tablets.
= 住在那座核电站附近的人都领到了碘化钾片。
potassium iodide = 碘化钾
② Silver iodide is sometimes sprayed into clouds to make it rain.
= 有时人们会把碘化银喷进云层里人工降雨。
silver iodide = 碘化银

iodine
/ˈaɪədiːn/
核心：碘；碘酒 —— 一种化学元素，人体必需的微量元素；也指涂伤口消毒用的碘酒。
① Iodine is added to salt to prevent health problems in children.
= 盐里加了碘，以防儿童出现健康问题。
iodine = 碘
② The nurse cleaned the cut on his knee with iodine.
= 护士用碘酒清洗了他膝盖上的伤口。
iodine = 碘酒

ion
/ˈaɪən/
核心：（物理、化学）离子 —— 失去或得到电子而带电的原子或分子。
形容词 ionic（离子的）、动词 ionize（使电离，英式也拼 -ise）、名词 ionization 与离子发生器 ionizer 并入本条。
① Salt breaks down into sodium and chloride ions in water.
= 盐在水中分解成钠离子和氯离子。
an ion = 离子
② Sodium chloride is held together by strong ionic bonds.
= 氯化钠靠很强的离子键结合在一起。
an ionic bond = 离子键
③ High-energy radiation can ionize the air around it.
= 高能辐射能使周围的空气电离。
ionize something = 使…电离
④ The ionization of gases makes neon signs glow.
= 气体的电离让霓虹灯发光。
ionization = 电离
⑤ She bought an ionizer to clean the air in her bedroom.
= 她买了一台负离子发生器来净化卧室的空气。
an ionizer = 负离子发生器

iota
/aɪˈəʊtə/
核心：极少量、一点点 —— 希腊字母表里最小的那个字母的名称，今天几乎只用在否定句里：not one iota（丝毫不）。
① His story has not changed one iota in twenty years.
= 二十年来，他的说法丝毫没变。
not one iota = 丝毫不
② There isn't an iota of truth in what the newspaper said about her.
= 报纸上关于她的说法没有一点点是真的。
not an iota of something = 一点…也没有

ipso facto
/ˌɪpsəʊ ˈfæktəʊ/
核心：（拉丁语，正式）根据该事实本身、当然地 —— 因为某个事实就自然得出某个结论。
① Being poor does not ipso facto make someone a criminal.
= 贫穷本身并不意味着一个人就是罪犯。
ipso facto = 就这一事实而言、当然
② The new rules mean that anyone over seventy is ipso facto excluded from the jury.
= 按新规定，任何七十岁以上的人都自然被排除在陪审团之外。
be ipso facto excluded = 当然被排除

Iranian
/ɪˈreɪniən/
核心：伊朗的；伊朗人。
① She cooked an Iranian dish of rice with saffron and dried fruit.
= 她做了一道加藏红花和干果的伊朗米饭。
Iranian food = 伊朗菜
② Many Iranians living abroad returned to vote in the election.
= 许多旅居海外的伊朗人回国参加了选举投票。
an Iranian = 伊朗人

Iraqi
/ɪˈrɑːki/
核心：伊拉克的；伊拉克人。
① The Iraqi government announced new elections for the spring.
= 伊拉克政府宣布春天举行新的选举。
the Iraqi government = 伊拉克政府
② An Iraqi who fled the war now runs a bakery in the town.
= 一个逃离战争的伊拉克人如今在镇上开了家面包店。
an Iraqi = 伊拉克人

irascible
/ɪˈræsəbəl/
核心：（正式）易怒的、脾气暴躁的 —— 一点小事就发火。名词 irascibility 并入本条。
① The irascible old judge often shouted at lawyers who were late.
= 那位脾气暴躁的老法官常对迟到的律师大吼。
an irascible old man = 暴躁的老人
② His irascibility grew worse as the pain in his back increased.
= 随着背痛加重，他的脾气越来越暴躁。
irascibility = 易怒

irate
/aɪˈreɪt/
核心：极为愤怒的 —— 比 angry 强，多说投诉的顾客、选民。
① Irate passengers surrounded the desk after their flight was cancelled.
= 航班取消后，愤怒的乘客围住了服务台。
irate passengers = 愤怒的乘客
② She received an irate phone call from a neighbour about the noise.
= 她接到邻居打来的一个怒气冲冲的电话，抱怨噪音。
an irate phone call = 怒气冲冲的电话

ire
/ˈaɪə(r)/
核心：（文）愤怒、怒火 —— 多用 draw / arouse somebody's ire（惹某人发怒）。
① The new tax drew the ire of farmers across the country.
= 新税激起了全国农民的怒火。
draw the ire of somebody = 惹某人发怒
② The referee's decision aroused the ire of the home fans.
= 裁判的判罚激怒了主队球迷。
arouse somebody's ire = 激怒某人

iridescent
/ˌɪrɪˈdesənt/
核心：彩虹色的、变色的 —— 随光线和角度变换颜色，如肥皂泡、孔雀羽毛。名词 iridescence 并入本条。
① In the sunlight the beetle's wings shone a beautiful iridescent green and blue.
= 阳光下，那只甲虫的翅膀闪着漂亮的虹彩般的绿色和蓝色。
iridescent = 虹彩色的
② In the garden the children were fascinated by the iridescence of the soap bubbles.
= 花园里，孩子们被肥皂泡的虹彩迷住了。
the iridescence of something = …的虹彩

iridology
/ˌɪrɪˈdɒlədʒi/
核心：虹膜诊断法 —— 通过观察眼睛虹膜来判断健康状况的另类疗法，科学界不认可。
① She paid a lot of money for iridology, but the doctor said it was nonsense.
= 她花大价钱做了虹膜诊断，可医生说那是无稽之谈。
iridology = 虹膜诊断法
② Iridology has never been shown to diagnose any disease reliably.
= 虹膜诊断法从来没被证明能可靠地诊断任何疾病。
iridology = 虹膜诊断法（另类疗法）

iris
/ˈaɪrɪs/
核心：（眼睛的）虹膜；鸢尾花。两个意思来源相同（希腊语「彩虹」）：眼球上有颜色的那一圈；
一种紫色或黄色的花。复数 irises。
① The colour of your eyes depends on the pigment in the iris.
= 眼睛的颜色取决于虹膜里的色素。
the iris = 虹膜
② Purple irises grew along the edge of the pond.
= 池塘边长着紫色的鸢尾花。
an iris = 鸢尾花

Irish
/ˈaɪrɪʃ/
核心：爱尔兰的；爱尔兰人（the Irish，复数）；爱尔兰语。
Irish coffee（爱尔兰咖啡，加威士忌和奶油的咖啡）并入本条。
① She has an Irish accent and grew up near Cork.
= 她有爱尔兰口音，在科克附近长大。
an Irish accent = 爱尔兰口音
② The Irish have a long tradition of storytelling.
= 爱尔兰人有悠久的讲故事传统。
the Irish = 爱尔兰人
③ Children in Ireland learn Irish at school alongside English.
= 爱尔兰的孩子在学校里既学英语也学爱尔兰语。
Irish = 爱尔兰语
④ After dinner we had an Irish coffee with thick cream on top.
= 晚饭后我们喝了杯上面盖着厚奶油的爱尔兰咖啡。
an Irish coffee = 爱尔兰咖啡
⑤ On cold winter evenings the pub serves a thick Irish stew of lamb, potatoes and onions.
= 冬天寒冷的晚上，那家酒馆供应一种浓稠的爱尔兰炖菜，用羊肉、土豆和洋葱炖成。
Irish stew = 爱尔兰炖菜
传统做法用羊肉，是爱尔兰的家常菜。
⑥ He ordered a glass of Irish whiskey and drank it slowly by the fire.
= 他点了一杯爱尔兰威士忌，坐在炉火旁慢慢地喝。
Irish whiskey = 爱尔兰威士忌
注意拼写：爱尔兰和美国的写作 whiskey，苏格兰的写作 whisky。

irk
/ɜːk/
核心：使恼火、使厌烦 —— 让人有点烦，程度比 annoy 轻。形容词 irksome（令人厌烦的）另立。
① It irks me when people talk loudly on their phones in trains.
= 有人在火车上大声打电话时，我就很恼火。
it irks somebody when = …让某人恼火
② The minister was clearly irked by the journalist's questions.
= 部长显然被记者的问题惹恼了。
be irked by something = 被…惹恼

irksome
/ˈɜːksəm/
核心：令人厌烦的、烦人的 —— 说事情、任务、规则让人不耐烦。
① Filling in forms is an irksome task that nobody enjoys.
= 填表是一件谁都不喜欢的烦人差事。
an irksome task = 烦人的差事
② She found the new rules about dress at work rather irksome.
= 她觉得公司关于着装的新规定相当烦人。
find something irksome = 觉得…烦人

iron
/ˈaɪən/
核心：铁；熨斗；熨烫。本义是铁这种金属（an iron gate）；由「铁」长出几支：
坚强、严厉的（an iron will、rule with an iron fist）；铁制的工具 —— 熨斗（动词 iron = 熨）、
（高尔夫）铁头球杆；复数 irons 指镣铐。短语与习语：iron out（解决、消除问题）、pump iron（练举重）、
strike while the iron is hot（趁热打铁）、have too many irons in the fire（同时做太多事）。
动名词 ironing 另立。
① The old farmhouse has a heavy iron gate at the entrance.
= 那座老农舍入口处有一扇沉重的铁门。
an iron gate = 铁门
② Spinach and red meat are good sources of iron.
= 菠菜和红肉是铁的良好来源。
iron = 铁（营养素）
③ She has an iron will and never gives up.
= 她意志坚强，从不放弃。
an iron will = 钢铁般的意志
④ The general ruled the country with an iron fist for thirty years.
= 那位将军用铁腕统治了那个国家三十年。
rule with an iron fist = 铁腕统治
⑤ Be careful when you put the iron away: it is still hot.
= 收熨斗时小心点，它还烫着。
an iron = 熨斗
⑥ He irons his shirts every Sunday evening for the week ahead.
= 他每个星期天晚上把接下来一周的衬衫都熨好。
iron a shirt = 熨衬衫
⑦ The two sides met to iron out their differences before signing the deal.
= 双方在签约前会面，消除分歧。
iron out differences = 消除分歧
⑧ He goes to the gym three times a week to pump iron.
= 他每周去三次健身房练举重。
pump iron = 练举重
⑨ The prices are low today, so strike while the iron is hot.
= 今天价钱低，要趁热打铁。
strike while the iron is hot = 趁热打铁
⑩ She has too many irons in the fire and never finishes anything.
= 她同时揽的事太多，什么都干不完。
have too many irons in the fire = 同时做太多事
⑪ The prisoner was brought into court in irons.
= 犯人戴着镣铐被带上法庭。
in irons = 戴着镣铐
⑫ He hit a seven iron onto the green.
= 他用七号铁杆把球打上了果岭。
an iron = （高尔夫）铁头球杆
⑬ Her grandfather had thick iron-grey hair and a voice that filled the whole church.
= 她祖父一头浓密的铁灰色头发，嗓音能响彻整座教堂。
iron-grey = 铁灰色的
多说头发、天空、海水；美式拼 iron-gray。
⑭ The soldiers carried iron rations of biscuits and tinned meat in case supplies ran out.
= 士兵们随身带着饼干和罐头肉作为应急口粮，以防补给断绝。
iron rations = 应急口粮
本义是军队的应急口粮；也谑指登山、远足时带的备用干粮。

ironclad
/ˈaɪənklæd/
核心：铁甲的；（比喻）坚不可摧的、无懈可击的。本义说十九世纪装铁甲的战舰；
比喻说保证、证据、协议牢靠得打不破（an ironclad guarantee）。
① The lawyer promised us an ironclad contract that nobody could break.
= 律师向我们保证了一份谁也打不破的合同。
an ironclad contract = 无懈可击的合同
② The museum has a model of an ironclad warship from the American Civil War.
= 博物馆里有一艘美国内战时期铁甲舰的模型。
an ironclad = 铁甲舰

ironic
/aɪˈrɒnɪk/
核心：讽刺的、反讽的；（事情）具有讽刺意味的。两支：说话故意说反话（an ironic smile）；
事情的结果与预期正好相反，让人哭笑不得（It is ironic that…）。副词 ironically 并入本条。
① It is ironic that the fire station burned down.
= 具有讽刺意味的是，消防站着火烧掉了。
it is ironic that = 具有讽刺意味的是…
② He gave an ironic smile when they called him a hero.
= 大家叫他英雄时，他报以一个讽刺的微笑。
an ironic smile = 讽刺的微笑
③ Ironically, the rain started just as the drought was declared over.
= 讽刺的是，刚宣布旱情结束，雨就下起来了。
ironically = 讽刺的是

ironing
/ˈaɪənɪŋ/
核心：熨衣服；（要熨或熨好的）衣物。不可数：do the ironing（熨衣服）。
ironing board（熨衣板）并入本条。
① I usually do the ironing on Sunday evening while listening to the radio.
= 我通常星期天晚上一边听收音机一边熨衣服。
do the ironing = 熨衣服
② There's a huge pile of ironing waiting for me in the bedroom.
= 卧室里有一大堆衣服等着我熨。
a pile of ironing = 一堆要熨的衣服
③ She set up the ironing board in the kitchen.
= 她在厨房里支起了熨衣板。
an ironing board = 熨衣板

ironmonger
/ˈaɪənmʌŋɡə(r)/
核心：（英，旧）五金商；五金店 —— 名词 ironmongery（五金器具；五金店）并入本条。
① The old ironmonger in the village sold everything from nails to buckets.
= 村里那家老五金店从钉子到水桶什么都卖。
an ironmonger = 五金商、五金店
② The shop stocks garden tools and household ironmongery.
= 那家店卖园艺工具和家用五金。
ironmongery = 五金器具

ironstone
/ˈaɪənstəʊn/
核心：铁矿石 —— 含铁量高的岩石；英国一些地区的房子用这种石头建成。
① The village church is built of local ironstone.
= 村里的教堂是用当地的铁矿石砌成的。
local ironstone = 当地的铁矿石
② The houses in the valley have a warm orange colour because of the ironstone.
= 因为用的是铁矿石，山谷里的房子呈现出温暖的橙色。
ironstone = 铁矿石

ironwork
/ˈaɪənwɜːk/
核心：铁制品、铁艺 —— 用铁做的装饰性栏杆、大门等。不可数。
① The balconies of the old houses in the square are decorated with fine ironwork.
= 广场上那些老房子的阳台装饰着精美的铁艺。
fine ironwork = 精美的铁艺
② Tourists come from all over the country to photograph the old bridge and its Victorian ironwork.
= 游客从全国各地赶来，拍那座老桥和桥上维多利亚时代的铁艺。
Victorian ironwork = 维多利亚时代的铁艺

ironworks
/ˈaɪənwɜːks/
核心：铸铁厂、炼铁厂 —— 单复同形。
① The town grew up around an ironworks built in the eighteenth century.
= 那个镇是围绕一座十八世纪建的炼铁厂发展起来的。
an ironworks = 炼铁厂
② The old ironworks is now a museum of industrial history.
= 那座旧炼铁厂现在是一座工业史博物馆。
the old ironworks = 旧炼铁厂

irony
/ˈaɪrəni/
核心：讽刺、反讽；具有讽刺意味的事。两支：说话用反话表达真意（say something with heavy irony）；
情况的结果与预期相反，令人哭笑不得（the irony is that…）。形容词 ironic 另立。
① "What lovely weather," he said with heavy irony as the rain poured down.
= 「天气真好啊。」大雨倾盆时，他满带讽刺地说。
with irony = 带着讽刺
② The irony is that the new motorway has made the traffic worse.
= 讽刺的是，新修的高速公路反倒让交通更糟了。
the irony is that = 讽刺的是
③ It was one of life's little ironies that she met her husband at a funeral.
= 人生真是有点讽刺，她是在一场葬礼上认识她丈夫的。
life's little ironies = 人生的小小讽刺

irradiate
/ɪˈreɪdieɪt/
核心：（用射线）照射、辐照；（文）照亮。本义是用放射线或紫外线处理东西（杀菌、保鲜、治病）；
文学上说光彩照亮（a face irradiated with joy）。名词 irradiation 并入本条。
① Some countries irradiate fruit and vegetables to kill bacteria and keep them fresh longer.
= 有些国家用射线辐照蔬果，以杀菌并延长保鲜期。
irradiate food = 辐照食品
这一支是技术用语，食品标签上常写 irradiated。
② The tumour was irradiated every day for six weeks at the city hospital.
= 在市医院，那个肿瘤连续六周每天接受放射治疗。
irradiate a tumour = 对肿瘤进行放射治疗
医学上多说 give radiotherapy，irradiate 更偏技术文字。
③ Her face was irradiated with joy when she saw her son at the airport gate.
= 在机场出口看到儿子时，她的脸上洋溢着喜悦的光彩。
be irradiated with joy = 洋溢着喜悦（文）
④ Food irradiation is still controversial, and many shoppers refuse to buy treated products.
= 食品辐照至今仍有争议，许多顾客拒绝购买经过辐照的产品。
irradiation = 辐照
不可数；医学上的放射治疗也可以叫 irradiation。

irrational
/ɪˈræʃənəl/
核心：不合理的、失去理智的 —— 不是根据道理而是凭感情、恐惧。数学上另指无理数（an irrational number）。
名词 irrationality 与副词 irrationally 并入本条。
① She has an irrational fear of birds and will not walk through the park alone.
= 她莫名其妙地怕鸟，不敢一个人穿过公园。
an irrational fear = 莫名的恐惧
常说恐惧、仇恨、行为「没有理由」，跟 illogical（推理不通）有分别。
② The square root of two is an irrational number, so its decimals never end.
= 二的平方根是无理数，小数永远写不完。
an irrational number = 无理数
数学术语，跟 rational number（有理数）相对。
③ Many economists pointed to the irrationality of the markets during the crisis.
= 许多经济学家指出了危机期间市场的非理性。
the irrationality of something = …的非理性
④ He behaved irrationally after the accident and shouted at the doctors who were helping him.
= 事故之后他举止失常，冲着正在救助他的医生大喊大叫。
irrationally = 失去理智地
常跟 behave、react、act 搭配。

irreconcilable
/ɪˌrekənˈsaɪləbəl/
核心：（正式）不可调和的、势不两立的 —— 说分歧、观点完全对立，无法和解。
① The couple divorced after twenty years, citing irreconcilable differences.
= 那对夫妻在结婚二十年后离了婚，理由是存在不可调和的分歧。
irreconcilable differences = 不可调和的分歧
离婚文书里的固定说法。
② The two parties hold irreconcilable views on the future of the railways.
= 两党在铁路的未来问题上持有截然对立的观点。
irreconcilable views = 截然对立的观点
也说 irreconcilable positions，多见于政治、宗教争论。

irrecoverable
/ˌɪrɪˈkʌvərəbəl/
核心：（正式）无法挽回的、不能收回的 —— 多说损失、债务、数据。副词 irrecoverably 并入本条。
① The bank wrote off the loan as an irrecoverable debt after the company went bankrupt.
= 那家公司破产后，银行把那笔贷款作为坏账注销了。
an irrecoverable debt = 无法收回的债务
会计用语，同 bad debt。
② Many of the old family photographs were irrecoverably damaged in the flood.
= 许多家族老照片在洪水中遭受了无法挽回的损坏。
irrecoverably damaged = 无法挽回地损坏
副词几乎只修饰 damaged、lost 这类词。

irredeemable
/ˌɪrɪˈdiːməbəl/
核心：（正式）无可救药的、无法挽回的；（债券）不能兑现的。副词 irredeemably 并入本条。
① Critics called the film an irredeemable failure with nothing to recommend it.
= 评论家说那部电影是彻头彻尾的失败，一无可取。
an irredeemable failure = 无可挽回的失败
说人或事坏到无法挽救，语气很重。
② By the end of the war, the old empire was irredeemably weakened.
= 到战争结束时，那个老帝国已经衰弱得无可挽回。
irredeemably = 无可挽回地
多修饰表示坏的形容词：irredeemably dull、irredeemably lost。
③ The government issued irredeemable bonds that paid interest but were never repaid.
= 政府发行了不可赎回的债券，只付利息、从不还本。
irredeemable bonds = 不可赎回的债券
金融术语，本义「不能赎回」。

irreducible
/ˌɪrɪˈdjuːsəbəl/
核心：（正式）不能再简化的、最低限度的 —— 已经到了不能再减少或再分的程度。副词 irreducibly 并入本条。
① Ten staff is the irreducible minimum needed to keep the hospital ward open at night.
= 要让那个病房夜里继续开着，十个员工是最低限度，不能再少。
the irreducible minimum = 最低限度
固定搭配，说「再少就不行了」的量。
② Some philosophers argue that human consciousness is irreducibly complex.
= 有些哲学家认为，人的意识复杂到无法再简化。
irreducibly = 不可简化地

irrefutable
/ˌɪrɪˈfjuːtəbəl/
核心：（正式）无可辩驳的、驳不倒的 —— 说证据、论点确凿。副词 irrefutably 并入本条。
① The DNA results provided irrefutable proof that he had been in the house that night.
= DNA 结果提供了无可辩驳的证据，证明他那晚到过那座房子。
irrefutable proof = 无可辩驳的证据
也说 irrefutable evidence / argument，比 undeniable 更书面。
② Her research shows irrefutably that the drug causes serious side effects in older patients.
= 她的研究无可辩驳地表明，那种药会在老年患者身上引起严重的副作用。
irrefutably = 无可辩驳地

irregular
/ɪˈreɡjʊlə(r)/
核心：不规则的、不整齐的；不定期的；不合规定的。几支：形状、表面不平整（an irregular shape）；
时间、间隔不固定（irregular meals）；不合常规、不合法的（irregular payments）；
语法上不按规则变化的（irregular verbs）；军事上的非正规部队（irregulars）。
名词 irregularity 与副词 irregularly 并入本条。
① The stones in the old wall are all irregular shapes and sizes.
= 那堵老墙上的石头都是大小形状不一的。
irregular shapes = 不规则的形状
第一支：形状、表面不整齐。
② Nurses who work nights often have irregular meals and poor sleep.
= 上夜班的护士常常吃饭不规律、睡眠不好。
irregular meals = 不规律的饮食
第二支：时间、间隔不固定，也说 irregular hours、irregular heartbeat。
③ Auditors found several irregular payments to a company owned by the director's brother.
= 审计员发现了几笔付给董事兄弟所开公司的违规款项。
irregular payments = 违规款项
第三支：不合规定，常暗示有问题，是委婉说法。
④ Students have to learn the past tense of irregular verbs such as go and take by heart.
= 学生们得把「go」「take」之类不规则动词的过去式背下来。
irregular verbs = 不规则动词
语法用语，跟 regular verbs（规则动词）相对。
⑤ The election was marked by serious irregularities, including missing ballot boxes.
= 那次选举存在严重的违规行为，包括投票箱失踪。
an irregularity = 违规之处、不规则之处
可数复数，多说选举、账目里的违规之处。
⑥ The patient's heart was beating irregularly, so the doctor ordered more tests.
= 病人的心跳不规律，医生于是要求做更多检查。
irregularly = 不规则地

irrelevant
/ɪˈreləvənt/
核心：无关的、不相干的；不重要的。常接 to。名词 irrelevance（无关紧要；无关的事）与副词 irrelevantly 并入本条。
① Your age is irrelevant to the job; what matters is whether you can do it well.
= 年龄跟这份工作无关，重要的是你能不能干好。
be irrelevant to something = 与…无关
介词用 to；比 have nothing to do with 正式。
② Many young people see the old political parties as increasingly irrelevant.
= 许多年轻人觉得那些老牌政党越来越无足轻重。
increasingly irrelevant = 越来越无足轻重
第二支：说人或机构跟不上时代、无足轻重。
③ The price of the tickets was an irrelevance, because everyone had been given free seats.
= 票价根本无关紧要，因为每个人都拿到了免费座位。
an irrelevance = 无关紧要的事
④ He talked irrelevantly about his holiday while we were trying to plan the budget.
= 我们正设法做预算时，他却东拉西扯地讲他的假期。
irrelevantly = 离题地
说话、写作扯到不相干的事上。

irreligious
/ˌɪrɪˈlɪdʒəs/
核心：（正式）不信宗教的；不敬神的。
① He grew up in an irreligious family and never went to church as a child.
= 他在一个不信教的家庭长大，小时候从没去过教堂。
an irreligious family = 不信教的家庭
中性，只说没有宗教信仰。
② The bishop condemned the play as irreligious and offensive to believers.
= 主教谴责那部剧对宗教不敬，冒犯了信徒。
irreligious = 不敬神的
这一支带贬义，多出自宗教人士之口。

irremediable
/ˌɪrɪˈmiːdiəbəl/
核心：（正式）无法补救的、不可挽回的 —— 损害、错误已经没法纠正。副词 irremediably 并入本条。
① The fire caused irremediable damage to the medieval paintings in the church.
= 那场火灾对教堂里的中世纪壁画造成了无法补救的损坏。
irremediable damage = 无法补救的损坏
比 irreparable 更正式，多见于法律、正式报告。
② Their friendship was irremediably damaged by the argument over the will.
= 那场关于遗嘱的争吵让他们的友谊受到了无法挽回的伤害。
irremediably = 无法补救地

irreparable
/ɪˈrepərəbəl/
核心：无法弥补的、不可挽回的 —— 损失、伤害大到修不好。副词 irreparably 并入本条。
① The scandal did irreparable harm to the company's reputation.
= 那起丑闻对公司的声誉造成了无法弥补的损害。
irreparable harm = 无法弥补的损害
常跟 damage、harm、loss 搭配。
② The old ship was irreparably damaged when it hit the rocks during the storm.
= 那艘旧船在暴风雨中触礁，损坏得无法修复。
irreparably damaged = 损坏得无法修复
副词多修饰 damaged、harmed、broken。

irreplaceable
/ˌɪrɪˈpleɪsəbəl/
核心：不可替代的 —— 丢了、坏了就再也找不到同样的；也说人独一无二、无人能顶替。
① Many of the letters lost in the fire were irreplaceable family records.
= 在火灾中烧掉的信件里，许多是无法替代的家族记录。
irreplaceable records = 无法替代的记录
说东西独一无二，丢了就再也找不回来。
② After thirty years at the school, the head teacher seemed irreplaceable to everyone.
= 那位校长在学校干了三十年，在大家眼里似乎无人能顶替。
be irreplaceable = 不可替代
说人时是很高的称赞；反过来 nobody is irreplaceable 是「谁都可以被替代」。

irrepressible
/ˌɪrɪˈpresəbəl/
核心：（人）活泼快乐、压抑不住的；（感情）抑制不住的。副词 irrepressibly 并入本条。
① Even in hospital, the irrepressible old man kept telling jokes to the nurses.
= 即使住在医院里，那位活泼开朗的老人还是不停地给护士讲笑话。
irrepressible = 活泼开朗、压抑不住的
说人时是褒义，指乐观、精力充沛，什么都压不住。
② The children were irrepressibly excited on the last day of term.
= 学期最后一天，孩子们兴奋得按捺不住。
irrepressibly excited = 兴奋得按捺不住
③ She felt an irrepressible urge to laugh during the serious speech.
= 在那场严肃的讲话中，她有一股忍不住想笑的冲动。
an irrepressible urge = 抑制不住的冲动
说感情时，常跟 urge、laughter、curiosity 搭配。

irreproachable
/ˌɪrɪˈprəʊtʃəbəl/
核心：（正式）无可指责的、无懈可击的 —— 说行为、品格、记录好得挑不出毛病。
① The judge had an irreproachable record after forty years on the bench.
= 那位法官在任四十年，记录无可指摘。
an irreproachable record = 无可指摘的记录
比 perfect 正式，多说品行、记录、举止。
② Her manners at the royal dinner were irreproachable.
= 她在王室晚宴上的举止无可挑剔。
irreproachable manners = 无可挑剔的举止

irresistible
/ˌɪrɪˈzɪstəbəl/
核心：不可抗拒的、极有诱惑力的 —— 强大到挡不住，或诱人得让人忍不住。副词 irresistibly 并入本条。
① The smell of fresh bread from the bakery was irresistible, so we bought two loaves.
= 面包店飘出的新鲜面包香味让人无法抗拒，于是我们买了两条。
be irresistible = 让人无法抗拒
常说食物、价钱、诱惑；也可说人很有魅力。
② She felt an irresistible urge to tell everyone the good news.
= 她有一股抑制不住的冲动，想把好消息告诉每个人。
an irresistible urge = 不可抗拒的冲动
跟 irrepressible urge 近义：irresistible 偏「挡不住外力」，irrepressible 偏「压不住自己」。
③ The children were irresistibly drawn to the ice cream van.
= 孩子们不由自主地被冰淇淋车吸引过去。
be irresistibly drawn to something = 不由自主地被…吸引
副词常修饰 drawn、attracted、funny。

irresolute
/ɪˈrezəluːt/
核心：（正式）犹豫不决的、优柔寡断的 —— 拿不定主意。副词 irresolutely 与名词 irresolution 并入本条。
① The irresolute leader waited too long, and the enemy crossed the river unopposed.
= 那位优柔寡断的领导等得太久，敌人毫无阻挡地过了河。
an irresolute leader = 优柔寡断的领导
比 indecisive 更书面。
② She stood irresolutely at the door, not knowing whether to knock.
= 她犹豫地站在门口，不知道该不该敲门。
irresolutely = 犹豫不决地
③ The government's irresolution over the new airport has delayed the project for years.
= 政府在新机场问题上的犹豫不决，让项目拖延了好几年。
irresolution = 犹豫不决
不可数，正式。

irrespective of
/ˌɪrɪˈspektɪv əv/
核心：不管、不论 —— 介词短语，同 regardless of，偏正式。
① The job is open to all applicants, irrespective of age or nationality.
= 这份工作对所有申请者开放，不论年龄或国籍。
irrespective of something = 不论…
介词短语，后面接名词或 whether 从句；同 regardless of，偏正式。
② The match will go ahead irrespective of the weather, even if it rains all day.
= 不管天气如何，比赛都照常进行，哪怕下一整天雨。
irrespective of the weather = 不管天气如何

irresponsible
/ˌɪrɪˈspɒnsəbəl/
核心：不负责任的 —— 做事不考虑后果。名词 irresponsibility 与副词 irresponsibly 并入本条。
① It was irresponsible of him to leave the children alone in the house all evening.
= 他把孩子们整晚单独留在家里，太不负责任了。
it was irresponsible of somebody to do something = 某人做…太不负责任
② The report criticized the bank's irresponsibility in lending money to people who could not repay it.
= 报告批评了那家银行放贷给还不起钱的人的不负责任做法。
irresponsibility = 不负责任
不可数，多说机构、政策。
③ Some drivers behave irresponsibly on the motorway, especially in bad weather.
= 有些司机在高速公路上开车不负责任，天气不好时尤其如此。
irresponsibly = 不负责任地
常修饰 behave、act、drive、spend。

irretrievable
/ˌɪrɪˈtriːvəbəl/
核心：（正式）无法挽回的、不能恢复的 —— 说损失、关系、数据。副词 irretrievably 并入本条。
① The judge accepted that the marriage had broken down irretrievably.
= 法官认定那段婚姻已经破裂到无法挽回。
break down irretrievably = 彻底破裂
离婚判决里的固定说法。
② Without a backup, the files are irretrievable once the disk fails.
= 没有备份的话，磁盘一坏，文件就无法恢复了。
be irretrievable = 无法恢复

irreverent
/ɪˈrevərənt/
核心：不敬的、不恭的 —— 对应当尊重的人或事不严肃，常带幽默、调侃，可褒可贬。
名词 irreverence 与副词 irreverently 并入本条。
① The magazine is famous for its irreverent jokes about politicians and the royal family.
= 那本杂志以拿政客和王室开不恭的玩笑而闻名。
irreverent jokes = 不恭的玩笑
不一定是贬义：常指对权威、传统开玩笑，带点俏皮。
② Young audiences loved the irreverence of the comedy, but older viewers complained.
= 年轻观众喜欢那部喜剧的玩世不恭，年长的观众却投诉了。
irreverence = 不恭
不可数；褒义时指一种轻松、不拘礼的幽默。
③ He spoke irreverently about the old traditions of the college.
= 他说起学院的老传统来毫无敬意。
irreverently = 不敬地

irreversible
/ˌɪrɪˈvɜːsəbəl/
核心：不可逆转的、无法挽回的 —— 变化一旦发生就回不去了。副词 irreversibly 并入本条。
① Smoking can cause irreversible damage to the lungs.
= 吸烟会对肺造成不可逆转的损害。
irreversible damage = 不可逆转的损害
多说健康、环境、气候上的损害。
② The decision to close the mine is irreversible, whatever the protesters say.
= 不管抗议者怎么说，关闭矿井的决定都不可更改。
be irreversible = 不可逆转
说决定时意思接近 irrevocable（不可撤销）。
③ The climate has been irreversibly changed by human activity.
= 人类活动已经让气候发生了不可逆转的变化。
irreversibly = 不可逆转地
常修饰 changed、damaged。

irrevocable
/ɪˈrevəkəbəl/
核心：（正式）不可撤销的、无法取消的 —— 决定、承诺一旦作出就不能收回。副词 irrevocably 并入本条。
① Signing the contract is an irrevocable decision, so read it carefully first.
= 签合同是一个不能反悔的决定，所以先仔细读一遍。
an irrevocable decision = 不可撤销的决定
也说 irrevocable step、irrevocable commitment；法律上指合同条款不可撤销。
② Their lives were changed irrevocably by the accident.
= 那次事故彻底改变了他们的生活。
irrevocably = 不可挽回地

irrigate
/ˈɪrɪɡeɪt/
核心：灌溉；（医学）冲洗。本义是给田地引水浇灌；医学上指用水或药液冲洗伤口、眼睛等。
名词 irrigation 并入本条。
① Farmers in the valley irrigate their fields with water from the mountain river.
= 山谷里的农民用山上流下的河水灌溉田地。
irrigate fields = 灌溉田地
② The nurse irrigated the wound with salt water before putting on a clean dressing.
= 护士先用盐水冲洗伤口，再换上干净的敷料。
irrigate a wound = 冲洗伤口
医学用法，正式。
③ Without irrigation, nothing would grow in this dry region.
= 没有灌溉，这个干旱地区什么也长不出来。
irrigation = 灌溉
④ The government built a huge irrigation system to bring water to the desert.
= 政府修建了一个庞大的灌溉系统，把水引到沙漠里。
an irrigation system = 灌溉系统

irritable
/ˈɪrɪtəbəl/
核心：易怒的、烦躁的；（医学）过敏的、易受刺激的。名词 irritability 与副词 irritably 并入本条；
irritable bowel syndrome（肠易激综合征，缩写「IBS」）也并在这里。
① He is always irritable in the morning until he has had his first cup of coffee.
= 他早上没喝第一杯咖啡之前总是脾气很躁。
be irritable = 烦躁、易怒
② Lack of sleep often causes irritability and poor concentration.
= 睡眠不足常会导致烦躁和注意力不集中。
irritability = 烦躁、易怒
③ "I've already told you twice," she said irritably, without looking up.
= 「我已经跟你说过两遍了。」她头也不抬，烦躁地说。
irritably = 烦躁地
④ She changed her diet after being diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome.
= 被诊断出肠易激综合征后，她改变了饮食。
irritable bowel syndrome = 肠易激综合征

irritant
/ˈɪrɪtənt/
核心：刺激物；让人恼火的事。两支：（医学、化学）刺激皮肤、眼睛等的物质；
比喻持续让人烦的人或事。
① Smoke is an irritant that can make your eyes water and your throat sore.
= 烟雾是一种刺激物，会让你流眼泪、嗓子疼。
an irritant = 刺激物
② The constant noise from the building site became a major irritant for local residents.
= 工地上没完没了的噪音成了当地居民的一大烦恼。
a major irritant = 一大烦恼

irritate
/ˈɪrɪteɪt/
核心：激怒、使烦躁；刺激（皮肤、眼睛）。两支：让人生气、心烦；身体部位受刺激发红发痒。
形容词 irritated（恼火的）、irritating（令人恼火的）、副词 irritatingly 与名词 irritation 并入本条。
① His habit of whistling while he worked really irritated his colleagues.
= 他边干活边吹口哨的习惯真让同事们恼火。
irritate somebody = 惹恼某人
② Some soaps can irritate sensitive skin and cause a rash.
= 有些肥皂会刺激敏感皮肤，引起皮疹。
irritate the skin = 刺激皮肤
这一义是医学、护肤用语，主语多是化学品、羊毛、阳光，宾语是皮肤、眼睛。
③ She was irritated by the long delay and asked to speak to the manager.
= 长时间的延误让她很恼火，她要求见经理。
be irritated by something = 被…惹恼
④ The most irritating thing about the new phone is that the battery runs out so quickly.
= 这部新手机最让人恼火的是电池掉得太快。
irritating = 令人恼火的
⑤ The instructions were irritatingly vague about how to connect the cables.
= 说明书对怎么连接电缆说得含糊不清，让人恼火。
irritatingly = 令人恼火地
⑥ He could not hide his irritation when the train was cancelled again.
= 火车又一次取消时，他掩饰不住心中的恼火。
irritation = 恼火
⑦ The cream will soothe any irritation caused by insect bites.
= 这种药膏能缓解虫咬引起的任何刺痒。
irritation = （皮肤等的）刺痒、发炎

irrupt
/ɪˈrʌpt/
核心：（正式）闯入、突然冲进；（感情、事件）突然爆发。名词 irruption 并入本条。
跟 erupt 读音相近：erupt 是从里往外喷，irrupt 是从外往里冲。
① Protesters irrupted into the meeting, shouting and waving banners.
= 抗议者冲进会场，高声叫喊、挥舞着横幅。
irrupt into something = 闯入…
② The sudden irruption of violence shocked the quiet town.
= 突如其来的暴力冲击了那个宁静的小镇。
an irruption of something = …的突然爆发

ischaemia
/ɪˈskiːmiə/
核心：（医学）缺血 —— 身体某部分血液供应不足。美式拼 ischemia。
① Ischaemia of the heart muscle can lead to chest pain and heart attacks.
= 心肌缺血会导致胸痛和心脏病发作。
ischaemia = 缺血
② The scan showed signs of ischaemia in the patient's left leg.
= 扫描显示病人左腿有缺血迹象。
signs of ischaemia = 缺血的迹象

ish
/ɪʃ/
核心：（口语）有点儿、大概 —— 单独成词使用，表示「差不多、不完全」，常放在句末或单独回答。
来自形容词、时间后面的后缀 -ish（sevenish、greenish），口语里独立成了一个词。
① "Are you ready?" "Ish. I just need to find my shoes."
= 「你准备好了吗？」「差不多吧，我就差找到鞋子了。」
ish = 差不多、有点儿
② The film was good, ish, but the ending was disappointing.
= 那部电影还算不错吧，只是结尾让人失望。
ish = 还算（带保留）

Islam
/ˈɪzlɑːm/
核心：伊斯兰教；伊斯兰世界 —— 信奉真主安拉、以《古兰经》为经典的宗教；也指穆斯林的整个世界。
① He converted to Islam when he was twenty-five.
= 他二十五岁时皈依了伊斯兰教。
convert to Islam = 皈依伊斯兰教
② The book describes the spread of Islam across North Africa in the seventh century.
= 那本书讲述了七世纪伊斯兰教在北非的传播。
the spread of Islam = 伊斯兰教的传播

Islamic
/ɪzˈlæmɪk/
核心：伊斯兰教的、伊斯兰的 —— 说宗教、艺术、法律、国家。
① The museum has a fine collection of Islamic art, including tiles and carpets.
= 那家博物馆藏有精美的伊斯兰艺术品，包括瓷砖和地毯。
Islamic art = 伊斯兰艺术
② The bank offers Islamic mortgages that do not charge interest.
= 那家银行提供不收利息的伊斯兰式按揭贷款。
Islamic finance = 伊斯兰金融

Islamism
/ˈɪzləmɪzəm/
核心：伊斯兰主义 —— 主张以伊斯兰教法治理国家和社会的政治思想。跟 Islam（宗教本身）要分清。
① The book examines the rise of Islamism in the Middle East in the 1970s.
= 那本书考察了二十世纪七十年代伊斯兰主义在中东的兴起。
the rise of Islamism = 伊斯兰主义的兴起
② Scholars disagree about how far Islamism is a religious or a political movement.
= 学者们对伊斯兰主义在多大程度上是宗教运动、多大程度上是政治运动看法不一。
Islamism = 伊斯兰主义

Islamist
/ˈɪzləmɪst/
核心：伊斯兰主义的；伊斯兰主义者 —— 支持伊斯兰主义的人或团体，新闻里常指激进派别。
① An Islamist party won the most seats in the election.
= 一个伊斯兰主义政党在选举中赢得了最多席位。
an Islamist party = 伊斯兰主义政党
② The report warns that some Islamists are recruiting young people online.
= 报告警告说，一些伊斯兰主义者正在网上招募年轻人。
an Islamist = 伊斯兰主义者

island
/ˈaɪlənd/
核心：岛；（比喻）孤立的地方或群体。本义是四面环水的陆地；比喻被周围隔开的地方（a traffic island，道路中间的安全岛）。
岛民 islander 与跳岛游 island-hopping 并入本条。
① They spent their holiday on a small island with no cars and only one shop.
= 他们在一个没有汽车、只有一家商店的小岛上度假。
on an island = 在岛上
介词用 on，不用 in。
② Pedestrians waited on the traffic island in the middle of the busy road.
= 行人在繁忙马路中间的安全岛上等着。
a traffic island = （道路中的）安全岛
③ The village felt like an island of calm in the middle of the noisy city.
= 那个村落就像喧嚣城市中的一个宁静孤岛。
an island of something = …的孤岛
④ The islanders depend on a ferry that runs only twice a week.
= 岛民们靠一艘每周只开两班的渡船出行。
an islander = 岛民
⑤ They went island-hopping around Greece for three weeks.
= 他们在希腊群岛间跳岛游了三个星期。
island-hopping = 跳岛游

isle
/aɪl/
核心：（文或用于地名）岛 —— 比 island 书面、诗意，今天多见于地名：the Isle of Man、the British Isles。
① They sailed to a tiny isle off the west coast of Scotland.
= 他们驶向苏格兰西海岸外的一个小岛。
an isle = 小岛（文）
② The British Isles include Great Britain, Ireland and many smaller islands.
= 不列颠群岛包括大不列颠岛、爱尔兰岛和许多更小的岛屿。
the British Isles = 不列颠群岛

islet
/ˈaɪlət/
核心：小岛 —— 很小的岛；也指（解剖）胰岛（islets of Langerhans）。
① Seabirds nest on the rocky islets around the bay.
= 海鸟在海湾周围多岩石的小岛上筑巢。
an islet = 小岛
② Diabetes develops when the islets in the pancreas stop producing insulin.
= 当胰腺里的胰岛停止分泌胰岛素时，就会得糖尿病。
islets = 胰岛

ism
/ˈɪzəm/
核心：（口语，常贬）主义、学说 —— 来自 communism、socialism 这类词的后缀，独立成词，常带不屑。
① He was tired of all the isms of politics and just wanted cheaper bread.
= 他厌倦了政治上的种种主义，只想面包便宜点。
isms = 种种主义
② She doesn't believe in any ism; she judges each problem on its own.
= 她不信奉任何主义，每个问题都单独看。
an ism = 某种主义

isobar
/ˈaɪsəbɑː(r)/
核心：（气象）等压线 —— 天气图上连接气压相同各点的线。
① On the weather map, the isobars were very close together, which meant strong winds.
= 天气图上等压线很密，这意味着风很大。
isobars = 等压线
② Forecasters draw isobars to show where high and low pressure systems are.
= 气象预报员画等压线来显示高压和低压系统的位置。
draw isobars = 画等压线

isolate
/ˈaɪsəleɪt/
核心：隔离、孤立；分离出。几支：把人与别人分开（isolate a patient）；让人或国家孤立无援；
（科学）把某种物质、病毒单独分离出来；找出问题所在（isolate the cause）。
形容词 isolated 另立；isolating（使人孤立的）并入本条。
① Patients with the disease are isolated to stop it spreading.
= 患这种病的病人被隔离，以防止传播。
isolate somebody = 隔离某人
② Scientists isolated the virus from blood samples in 1983.
= 科学家于一九八三年从血样中分离出了这种病毒。
isolate a virus = 分离病毒
③ Engineers are trying to isolate the cause of the power failure.
= 工程师们正设法找出停电的原因。
isolate the cause = 找出原因
④ Working from home can be isolating for people who live alone.
= 对独居的人来说，在家工作可能让人感到孤立。
isolating = 使人感到孤立的

isolated
/ˈaɪsəleɪtɪd/
核心：孤立的、偏远的；个别的。两支：地方偏僻、人孤单（an isolated village、feel isolated）；
事情是单独发生的、不成规律的（an isolated incident）。
① They live in an isolated farmhouse miles from the nearest road.
= 他们住在一座偏僻的农舍里，离最近的公路有好几英里。
an isolated farmhouse = 偏僻的农舍
② Many elderly people feel isolated after their partner dies.
= 许多老人在伴侣去世后感到孤独。
feel isolated = 感到孤独
③ The police say the attack was an isolated incident and the area is safe.
= 警方说那次袭击是个别事件，这一带是安全的。
an isolated incident = 个别事件

isolation
/ˌaɪsəˈleɪʃən/
核心：隔离；孤立、孤独。几支：为防传染把人分开（in isolation）；与外界隔绝的状态；
孤独感；in isolation 也指「孤立地（看问题）」。
① The patient was kept in isolation for two weeks.
= 那位病人被隔离了两周。
in isolation = 在隔离中
② After moving to the countryside, she suffered from a sense of isolation.
= 搬到乡下以后，她深受孤独感之苦。
a sense of isolation = 孤独感
③ These figures should not be looked at in isolation, but compared with last year's.
= 这些数字不应孤立地看，而应与去年的比较。
in isolation = 孤立地
④ The country's isolation grew after it left the trade agreement.
= 那个国家退出贸易协定后，更加孤立了。
somebody's isolation = 某人的孤立

isolationism
/ˌaɪsəˈleɪʃənɪzəm/
核心：孤立主义 —— 主张国家不参与国际事务、不结盟的外交政策。孤立主义者 isolationist（也作形容词）并入本条。
① American isolationism kept the country out of the war until 1941.
= 美国的孤立主义让它直到一九四一年才参战。
isolationism = 孤立主义
② Isolationists in parliament voted against sending troops abroad.
= 议会里的孤立主义者投票反对向国外派兵。
an isolationist = 孤立主义者
③ The new president's isolationist policies worried the country's allies.
= 新总统的孤立主义政策让盟国感到不安。
isolationist policies = 孤立主义政策

isomer
/ˈaɪsəmə(r)/
核心：（化学）同分异构体 —— 分子式相同、原子排列不同、性质也不同的化合物。
形容词 isomeric 与名词 isomerism（同分异构现象）并入本条。
① Glucose and fructose are isomers: they contain the same atoms arranged differently.
= 葡萄糖和果糖是同分异构体：它们含有相同的原子，只是排列不同。
an isomer = 同分异构体
② The two isomeric forms of the drug have very different effects on the body.
= 这种药的两种同分异构形式对身体的作用大不相同。
isomeric forms = 同分异构形式
③ Students learn about isomerism in their second year of chemistry.
= 学生们在化学课第二年学习同分异构现象。
isomerism = 同分异构现象

isometric
/ˌaɪsəʊˈmetrɪk/
核心：等长收缩的（肌肉锻炼）；等距的、等轴的（绘图）。名词复数 isometrics（等长练习）并入本条。
① Isometric exercises strengthen muscles without moving the joints.
= 等长练习能在关节不动的情况下增强肌肉力量。
isometric exercises = 等长练习
② The architect showed us an isometric drawing of the new kitchen.
= 建筑师给我们看了新厨房的等轴测图。
an isometric drawing = 等轴测图
③ After the injury, her physiotherapist started her on gentle isometrics.
= 受伤后，她的理疗师让她从轻柔的等长练习开始。
isometrics = 等长练习

isotherm
/ˈaɪsəθɜːm/
核心：（气象）等温线 —— 地图上连接气温相同各点的线。
① The isotherms on the map show how quickly the temperature drops towards the north.
= 地图上的等温线显示出越往北气温下降得多快。
isotherms = 等温线
② Along the zero-degree isotherm, rain turns to snow.
= 在零度等温线一带，雨会变成雪。
the zero-degree isotherm = 零度等温线

isotonic
/ˌaɪsəˈtɒnɪk/
核心：等渗的 —— 说运动饮料等与人体体液浓度相同、易吸收的。
① Runners often drink isotonic sports drinks to replace lost salts.
= 跑步的人常喝等渗运动饮料来补充流失的盐分。
an isotonic drink = 等渗饮料
② The doctor gave the patient an isotonic solution through a drip.
= 医生通过点滴给病人输了等渗溶液。
an isotonic solution = 等渗溶液

isotope
/ˈaɪsətəʊp/
核心：（化学、物理）同位素 —— 同一元素中质子数相同、中子数不同的原子，有的具放射性。
① Carbon-14 is a radioactive isotope used to find the age of ancient objects.
= 碳十四是一种放射性同位素，用来测定古物的年代。
a radioactive isotope = 放射性同位素
② Doctors use tiny amounts of isotopes to trace how blood moves through the body.
= 医生用微量的同位素追踪血液在体内的流动。
isotopes = 同位素

Israeli
/ɪzˈreɪli/
核心：以色列的；以色列人 —— 指现代以色列国及其国民。注意与 Israelite（古代以色列人）区分。
① The Israeli government announced new elections for the autumn.
= 以色列政府宣布秋季举行新的选举。
the Israeli government = 以色列政府
② A group of young Israelis were travelling around South America after their military service.
= 一群服完兵役的以色列年轻人正在南美洲旅行。
an Israeli = 以色列人

Israelite
/ˈɪzrəlaɪt/
核心：（历史）古以色列人 —— 《圣经》里雅各的后代，古代以色列王国的人民。跟 Israeli（现代以色列人）不同。
① The story tells how the Israelites escaped from Egypt.
= 那个故事讲的是古以色列人怎样逃出埃及。
the Israelites = 古以色列人
② An Israelite king built the first temple in Jerusalem, according to the Bible.
= 据《圣经》记载，一位古以色列国王在耶路撒冷修建了第一座圣殿。
an Israelite king = 古以色列国王

issue
/ˈɪʃuː/
核心：本义是「流出、发出」。由此长出两大支：
一是名词「议题、问题」—— 大家要讨论、有争议的事（a political issue、the issue of…），口语里也指「毛病、麻烦」（have issues with）；
at issue（争论中的）、take issue with（对…提出异议）、make an issue of（小题大做）；
二是「发出、发行」—— 动词：正式发出、分发（issue a statement / passports）；名词：一期（杂志、报纸）、一次发行（an issue of stamps）；
（旧，法律）子女、后代。issue from（从…流出、源于）与发行人 issuer 并入本条。
① Climate change has become a major political issue in many countries.
= 在许多国家，气候变化已经成为一个重大的政治议题。
a political issue = 政治议题
② The meeting discussed the issue of rising rents in the city centre.
= 会议讨论了市中心租金上涨的问题。
the issue of something = …的问题
③ The point at issue is whether the council knew about the danger.
= 争论的焦点是市政会是否知道那个危险。
at issue = 争论中的、讨论中的
④ I take issue with your claim that young people don't read any more.
= 我不同意你说的年轻人不再读书了。
take issue with something = 对…提出异议
⑤ He was late again, but I didn't want to make an issue of it in front of the others.
= 他又迟到了，但我不想当着别人的面小题大做。
make an issue of something = 小题大做
⑥ My laptop has some issues with the battery, so I'm getting it repaired.
= 我的笔记本电脑电池有点毛病，我正拿去修。
have issues with something = …有毛病（口语）
⑦ The government issued a warning about the heatwave.
= 政府发出了热浪预警。
issue a warning = 发出警告
⑧ All visitors are issued with a pass at the front desk.
= 所有访客都在前台领到一张通行证。
be issued with something = 领到…
⑨ The article appeared in the March issue of the magazine.
= 那篇文章刊登在杂志的三月号上。
an issue of a magazine = 一期杂志
⑩ The post office announced a special issue of stamps for the royal wedding.
= 邮局宣布为王室婚礼发行一套特种邮票。
an issue of stamps = 一次邮票发行
⑪ Strange noises issued from the old house at night.
= 夜里，那座老房子里传出奇怪的声音。
issue from something = 从…传出、流出
⑫ The bank is the issuer of the card and is responsible for any fraud.
= 那家银行是这张卡的发卡机构，要对任何欺诈负责。
the issuer of something = …的发行人
⑬ He died without issue, so his estate went to his nephew.
= 他死时没有子嗣，于是遗产归了他的侄子。
without issue = 无子嗣（旧，法律）
⑭ Parking was a non-issue in the street until the flats were built opposite.
= 对面那些公寓盖起来以前，这条街上停车根本不成问题。
a non-issue = 不成问题的事
⑮ The bank raised money through a rights issue to its shareholders.
= 那家银行通过向股东配股筹集了资金。
a rights issue = 配股

isthmus
/ˈɪsθməs/
核心：地峡 —— 连接两块大陆地、两边是水的狭长陆地。
① The Isthmus of Panama joins North and South America.
= 巴拿马地峡连接着北美洲和南美洲。
the Isthmus of Panama = 巴拿马地峡
② The old town was built on a narrow isthmus between the lake and the sea.
= 那座古镇建在湖海之间一片狭长的地峡上。
a narrow isthmus = 狭长的地峡

it
/ɪt/
核心：它 —— 代词，本义指已经提到或眼前的东西、动物、情况。由此长出几个不指具体东西的用法：
占位主语 —— 说天气、时间、距离（it's raining、it's five o'clock）；
形式主语 / 宾语 —— 把后面的不定式、从句挪到句尾（It is important to…、I find it hard to…）；
强调句 —— It was John who…；口语习语：that's it（就这样；够了）、this is it（关键时刻到了）、
it's time（该…了）。缩约形式 it's（it is / it has）、it'd（it would / it had）、it'll（it will）并入本条。
注意别混：it's 是缩约，its 是物主形式，另立一条。
① I bought a new lamp, but it doesn't give enough light for reading.
= 我买了一盏新灯，可它的光不够读书。
it = 它
② It's been raining all morning, so the match might be cancelled.
= 下了一上午雨，比赛可能要取消了。
it's raining = 下雨了
说天气、时间时的占位主语，没有实际所指。
③ It is important to drink plenty of water when you have a fever.
= 发烧时多喝水很重要。
it is important to do something = 做…很重要
形式主语：真正的主语是后面的不定式。
④ She found it hard to sleep after the accident.
= 事故之后，她觉得很难入睡。
find it hard to do something = 觉得做…很难
形式宾语。
⑤ It was my sister who called the ambulance, not me.
= 叫救护车的是我姐姐，不是我。
it was somebody who = 是某人…（强调句）
⑥ That's it for today; we'll finish the chapter tomorrow.
= 今天就到这儿，明天我们把这一章讲完。
that's it = 就这样、到此为止
⑦ The door opened and the judges walked in; this was it.
= 门开了，评委们走了进来，关键时刻到了。
this is it = 关键时刻到了
⑧ It's time we went home; the last bus leaves in ten minutes.
= 我们该回家了，末班车十分钟后开。
it's time = 该…了
后面接过去时从句或不定式。
⑨ It'll be dark soon, so we'd better start walking back.
= 天快黑了，我们最好开始往回走。
it'll = it will
⑩ It'd be a good idea to book a table before Friday.
= 星期五之前订张桌子会是个好主意。
it'd = it would / it had
⑪ It's been three years since we last met.
= 我们上次见面已经是三年前的事了。
it's = it is / it has

Italian
/ɪˈtæljən/
核心：意大利的；意大利人；意大利语。
① We had dinner at a small Italian restaurant near the station.
= 我们在车站附近一家意大利小餐馆吃了晚饭。
an Italian restaurant = 意大利餐馆
② Her grandparents were Italians who moved to Scotland in the 1950s.
= 她的祖父母是二十世纪五十年代搬到苏格兰的意大利人。
an Italian = 意大利人
③ She is learning Italian because she wants to study music in Rome.
= 她在学意大利语，因为她想去罗马学音乐。
Italian = 意大利语

Italianate
/ɪˈtæliəneɪt/
核心：意大利风格的 —— 多说建筑、园林模仿意大利式样。
① The house has an Italianate tower and a garden full of statues.
= 那座房子有一座意大利式的塔楼，花园里满是雕像。
an Italianate tower = 意大利式塔楼
② Many Victorian villas were built in the Italianate style.
= 许多维多利亚时代的别墅是按意大利风格建造的。
the Italianate style = 意大利风格

italic
/ɪˈtælɪk/
核心：斜体的 —— 字母向右倾斜的印刷字体。名词复数 italics（斜体字：in italics）与动词 italicize（用斜体排印）并入本条。
① The titles of books are usually printed in italic type.
= 书名通常用斜体印刷。
italic type = 斜体字
② The foreign words in the text are in italics.
= 文中的外来词用的是斜体。
in italics = 用斜体
③ Please italicize the names of ships and newspapers in your essay.
= 请在你的文章里把船名和报纸名改成斜体。
italicize something = 把…排成斜体

itch
/ɪtʃ/
核心：痒；渴望。本义是皮肤发痒、想挠（an itch on my back）；比喻心里痒痒、很想做某事
（an itch to travel、be itching to do）。形容词 itchy（发痒的）与名词 itchiness 并入本条；
itchy feet（英，口语）是「想到处走、坐不住」。
① The mosquito bite on my arm itched all night.
= 我胳膊上被蚊子咬的包痒了一整夜。
itch = 发痒
② I've got an itch in the middle of my back that I can't reach.
= 我背中间痒，够不着。
an itch = 痒
③ The children were itching to open their presents.
= 孩子们迫不及待地想拆礼物。
be itching to do something = 迫不及待想做…
④ After a year in the office, she had an itch to travel again.
= 在办公室待了一年后，她又心痒痒想去旅行了。
an itch to do something = 做…的渴望
⑤ This wool sweater is warm but a bit itchy.
= 这件羊毛衫很暖和，就是有点扎人。
itchy = 刺痒的
⑥ The cream soothes the itchiness caused by insect bites.
= 这种药膏能缓解虫咬引起的瘙痒。
itchiness = 瘙痒
⑦ After two years in the same town, he got itchy feet and moved to Spain.
= 在同一个镇上住了两年后，他坐不住了，搬去了西班牙。
itchy feet = （英）坐不住、想到处走

item
/ˈaɪtəm/
核心：一件、一项、一条。本义是清单里的一项：物品（an item of clothing）、议程上的一项、账单上的一笔、
新闻里的一条（a news item）；口语里 be an item 是「成了一对（恋人）」。
① The first item on the agenda is the budget for next year.
= 议程上的第一项是明年的预算。
an item on the agenda = 议程上的一项
② Police found several items of stolen jewellery in his car.
= 警察在他车里发现了几件被盗的珠宝。
an item of something = 一件…
③ There was a short item about the festival on the local news.
= 当地新闻里有一条关于那个节日的简短报道。
a news item = 一条新闻
④ Are those two an item now? They were holding hands at the party.
= 那两个人现在是一对了吗？他们在聚会上手牵着手。
be an item = 成了一对（口语）

itemize
/ˈaɪtəmaɪz/
核心：逐条列出、分项开列 —— 英式也拼 -ise；多说账单、费用清单。
① Please itemize all your travel expenses on the form.
= 请在表格上逐项列出你所有的差旅费用。
itemize expenses = 分项列出费用
② The phone bill is itemized, so you can see the cost of every call.
= 电话账单是逐项列出的，所以你能看到每一通电话的费用。
an itemized bill = 分项账单

iterate
/ˈɪtəreɪt/
核心：（正式）重复、反复做；（计算机、数学）迭代。名词 iteration（重复；迭代；一个版本）
与形容词 iterative（反复的、迭代的）并入本条。
① The software iterates through the list until it finds a match.
= 软件把列表反复过一遍，直到找到匹配项。
iterate through something = 逐个遍历…
② The designers improved the product through several iterations.
= 设计师们经过几轮迭代改进了产品。
an iteration = 一轮迭代、一个版本
③ Writing a good essay is an iterative process of drafting and rewriting.
= 写好一篇文章是一个反复起草、修改的过程。
an iterative process = 反复的过程

itinerant
/aɪˈtɪnərənt/
核心：（正式）巡回的、流动的 —— 从一地到另一地谋生或工作的。也作名词：流动工人、巡回者。
① In the past, itinerant farm workers moved from farm to farm at harvest time.
= 过去，流动的农场工人在收获季节从一个农场转到另一个农场。
itinerant workers = 流动工人
② An itinerant preacher arrived in the village and spoke in the market square.
= 一位巡回传教士来到村里，在集市广场上布道。
an itinerant preacher = 巡回传教士

itinerary
/aɪˈtɪnərəri/
核心：行程、旅行路线 —— 一次旅行的计划安排，包括去哪里、什么时候到。
① The travel agent sent us a detailed itinerary for our trip to Japan.
= 旅行社给我们寄来了去日本旅行的详细行程。
a detailed itinerary = 详细行程
② A visit to the old castle is on the itinerary for the second day.
= 参观古堡安排在第二天的行程里。
be on the itinerary = 在行程安排里

its
/ɪts/
核心：它的 —— it 的物主形式，没有撇号。最常见的拼写错误就是把它和 it's（it is / it has）弄混。
① The company has changed its name and moved its offices to Manchester.
= 那家公司改了名，还把办公室搬到了曼彻斯特。
its = 它的
② The dog wagged its tail when it saw the children coming home from school.
= 那条狗看到孩子们放学回家，摇起了尾巴。
its tail = 它的尾巴

itself
/ɪtˈself/
核心：它自己、它本身 —— 反身代词（The cat washed itself）；强调用法（the house itself）；
by itself（自动地；单独地）、in itself（本身、就其本身而言）。
① The cat was sitting in the sun, washing itself.
= 那只猫坐在阳光下，舔洗自己。
wash itself = 舔洗自己
反身用法。
② The village itself is quiet, but the beach nearby gets very busy.
= 村子本身很安静，但附近的海滩很热闹。
the something itself = …本身
强调用法，放在名词后面。
③ The door opened by itself, and a cold wind blew in.
= 门自己开了，一阵冷风吹了进来。
by itself = 自动地
④ The money isn't important in itself; what matters is that he apologized.
= 钱本身并不重要，重要的是他道了歉。
in itself = 本身、就其本身而言

ivory

jab
/dʒæb/
核心：（用尖东西或拳头）戳、捅；（拳击）刺拳；（英，口语）打针。名词动词同形。
几支：用手指、胳膊肘、尖东西快速地戳（jab somebody in the ribs）；拳击里短而快的直拳；
英式口语指预防针（a flu jab）；比喻尖刻的话（a jab at the government）。

jack
/dʒæk/
核心：本义是男子名 Jack，由「普通男人、干粗活的人」长出一串指工具、小东西的名词：
千斤顶（a car jack）；（纸牌）J（the jack of spades）；（电）插座、插孔（a phone jack），jack plug 是插头；
（滚木球）目标小球；（美，俚）一点也不（jack shit，粗俗）。
动词：jack up（用千斤顶顶起；抬高价格）、jack in（英，俚：放弃工作）、jack into（接入网络）、
jack off（粗俗：手淫）、jack around（美，俚：瞎混；耍弄某人）。
复合词 jack-in-the-box（玩偶匣）、jack-o'-lantern（南瓜灯）、Jack cheese（美，蒙特雷杰克奶酪）并入本条；
习语 jack of all trades（样样通、样样松的人）。
① He used a jack to lift the car and change the flat tyre.
= 他用千斤顶把车顶起来，换了那个瘪了的轮胎。
a car jack = 汽车千斤顶
② She laid down the jack of hearts and won the game.
= 她打出一张红桃J，赢了那一局。
the jack of hearts = 红桃J
③ Plug the headphones into the jack on the side of the computer.
= 把耳机插进电脑侧面的插孔里。
a headphone jack = 耳机插孔
a jack plug = 插头
④ They jacked up the car so they could look underneath it.
= 他们用千斤顶把车顶起来，好看看车底。
jack up a car = 用千斤顶顶起汽车
⑤ The hotels jack up their prices during the festival.
= 节日期间各家酒店都会抬高价格。
jack up prices = 抬高价格
⑥ He jacked in his job at the bank to become a musician.
= 他辞掉了银行的工作去当音乐人。
jack something in = （英，俚）放弃
⑦ In the film, the hacker jacks into the network through a cable in his neck.
= 电影里，那个黑客通过脖子上的一根线缆接入网络。
jack into something = （俚）接入（网络）
⑧ Stop jacking me around and tell me when the car will be ready.
= 别再耍我了，告诉我车什么时候能修好。
jack somebody around = （美，俚）耍弄某人
⑨ The boys were caught jacking off behind the bike sheds.
= 那几个男孩在自行车棚后面手淫被逮了个正着。
jack off = （粗俗）手淫
语域：粗俗，只在极随便的场合说。
⑩ He knows jack shit about cars, so don't ask him.
= 他对车一窍不通，别问他。
jack shit = （美，粗俗）什么也不
⑪ The child laughed as the jack-in-the-box sprang out of its box.
= 玩偶匣里的小人弹出来，孩子哈哈大笑。
a jack-in-the-box = 玩偶匣
⑫ The children carved a jack-o'-lantern for Halloween.
= 孩子们为万圣节刻了一个南瓜灯。
a jack-o'-lantern = 南瓜灯
⑬ She melted Jack cheese over the tortillas.
= 她把蒙特雷杰克奶酪熔化在玉米饼上。
Jack cheese = （美）蒙特雷杰克奶酪
⑭ My uncle can fix anything, but he's a jack of all trades and master of none.
= 我叔叔什么都会修，可样样通、样样松。
a jack of all trades = 样样都会一点的人
